title.en: Volume 105 Biographies 55: Yu Wenrong, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong
title.raw: 卷一百〇五 列傳第五十五: 宇文融 韋堅 楊慎矜 王鉷 Volume 105 Biographies 55: Yu Wenrong, Wei Jian, Yang Shenjin, Wang Hong

sentences.zh: 馮盎，高州良德人也。

translations.literal: Feng Ang, native of Liangde in Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang was a native of Liangde in Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 累代為本部大首領。

translations.literal: For successive generations his family had been the great chieftains of their native tribe.
translations.idiomatic: For generation after generation his clan had served as the great chieftains of the local tribe.

sentences.zh: 盎少有武略，隋開皇中為宋康令。

translations.literal: Ang showed military talent from youth; during the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as magistrate of Songkang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ang showed martial ability; under Emperor Wen of Sui in the Kaihuang period he was appointed magistrate of Songkang.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，潮、成等五州獠叛，盎馳至京，請討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou reign, the Liao of Chao, Cheng, and four other prefectures rebelled; Ang raced to the capital to request permission to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou era the Liao tribes of Chao, Cheng, and four other prefectures rose in revolt; Ang hurried to the capital and asked leave to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 文帝敕左僕射楊素與盎論賊形勢，素曰：「不意蠻夷中有此人，大可奇也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered the Left Vice Director Yang Su to discuss the rebels' situation with Ang; Su said: "I did not expect to find such a man among the frontier barbarians — most remarkable."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ordered the Left Vice Director Yang Su to confer with Ang on the rebels' dispositions. Su remarked, "To find such a man among the southern tribes is truly extraordinary."

sentences.zh: 即令盎發江、嶺兵擊之。

translations.literal: He then ordered Ang to mobilize troops from the Yangzi and Lingnan regions to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: At once he directed Ang to raise forces from the river counties and the Lingnan commanderies to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授金紫光祿大夫，仍除漢陽太守。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Ang was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently made Administrator of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were subdued, he received the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and was also installed as Administrator of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，廣、新二州賊帥高法澄、洗寶徹等並受林士弘節度，殺害隋官吏，盎率兵擊破之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, the bandit leaders Gao Facheng and Xian Baochè of Guang and Xin prefectures, both under the command of Lin Shihong, killed Sui officials; Ang led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 the rebel chiefs Gao Facheng and Xian Baochè in Guang and Xin, acting under Lin Shihong, slew Sui officials; Ang marched out and routed them.

sentences.zh: 既而寶徹兄子智臣又聚兵於新州，自為渠帥，盎趨往擊之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Baochè's nephew Zhichen again gathered forces in Xin Prefecture and declared himself chieftain; Ang hastened to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Baochè's nephew Zhichen mustered troops in Xin Prefecture and set himself up as bandit chief; Ang rushed to engage him.

sentences.zh: 兵交，盎卻兜鍪大呼曰：「爾等頗識我否？」

translations.literal: When battle was joined, Ang removed his helmet and shouted: "Do you fellows recognize me?"
translations.idiomatic: As the armies clashed, Ang pulled off his helmet and cried out, "Do any of you know who I am?"

sentences.zh: 賊多棄戈肉袒而拜，其徒遂潰，擒寶徹、智臣等，嶺外遂定。

translations.literal: Most of the rebels threw down their weapons, bared their torsos, and bowed; their followers scattered, and Baochè, Zhichen, and others were captured — the region beyond the mountains was thus secured.
translations.idiomatic: Many rebels cast aside their weapons, bared their chests, and prostrated themselves; the rest broke and fled. Baochè, Zhichen, and others were taken prisoner, and the Lingnan frontier was pacified.

sentences.zh: 或有說盎曰：「自隋季崩離，海內騷動。

translations.literal: Someone urged Ang, saying: "Since the collapse of the Sui, the realm has been in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Ang, "Ever since the fall of the Sui the empire has been in uproar.

sentences.zh: 今唐雖應運，而風教未浹，南越一隅，未有所定。

translations.literal: Although Tang now holds the Mandate, its civilizing influence has not yet penetrated; the corner of southern Yue remains unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Tang now possess Heaven's mandate, their transforming influence has not yet spread; the southern lands are still unconquered.

sentences.zh: 公克平五嶺二十余州，豈與趙佗九郡相比？

translations.literal: You have subjugated more than twenty prefectures of the Five Mountains — are you not the equal of Zhao Tuo's nine commanderies?
translations.idiomatic: You have pacified more than twenty prefectures across the Five Ridges — how does that compare to Zhao Tuo's nine commanderies?

sentences.zh: 今請上南越王之號。」

translations.literal: We now ask you to assume the title King of Southern Yue."
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to take for yourself the title King of Southern Yue."

sentences.zh: 盎曰：「吾居南越，於茲五代，本州牧伯，唯我一門，子女玉帛，吾之有也。

translations.literal: Ang replied: "I have dwelt in southern Yue for five generations; of the prefectural governors here, only my house remains — wives, children, jade, and silks, all are mine already.
translations.idiomatic: Ang answered, "My family has ruled southern Yue for five generations. I alone among the prefects of this region hold sway — sons and daughters, jade and silk, all are already mine.

sentences.zh: 人生富貴，如我殆難，常恐弗克負荷，以墜先業。

translations.literal: Few men attain wealth and honor such as mine; I constantly fear I cannot bear the burden and will ruin the work of my forefathers.
translations.idiomatic: Few men enjoy wealth and status like mine; I often fear I cannot sustain it and will ruin my ancestors' estate.

sentences.zh: 本州衣錦便足，余復何求？

translations.literal: To return home in embroidered robes is enough — what more could I seek?
translations.idiomatic: Returning home in glory is enough for me — what more could I want?

sentences.zh: 越王之號，非所聞也。」

translations.literal: The title King of Southern Yue is something I have never heard of."
translations.idiomatic: The title King of Southern Yue is not for me to accept."

sentences.zh: 四年，盎以南越之眾降，高祖以其地為羅、春、白、崖、儋、林等八州，仍授盎上柱國、高羅總管，封吳國公，尋改封越國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Ang surrendered with the forces of southern Yue; Gaozu made his territory into eight prefectures — Luo, Chun, Bai, Ya, Dan, Lin, and others — and appointed Ang Superior Pillar of State and Commander-in-Chief of Gaoluo, enfeoffing him as Duke of Wu, then changing the fief to Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Ang submitted with the armies of southern Yue. Gaozu organized his territory into eight prefectures — Luo, Chun, Bai, Ya, Dan, Lin, and others — and made Ang Superior Pillar of State and overall commander of Gaoluo, enfeoffing him as Duke of Wu, soon afterward retitling him Duke of Yue.

sentences.zh: 拜其子智戴為春州刺史，智或東合州刺史，徙封盎耿國公。

translations.literal: His son Zhidai was appointed Prefect of Chunzhou, Zhihuo Prefect of Donghe, and Ang's fief was transferred to Duke of Geng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhidai was made Prefect of Chun, Zhihuo Prefect of Donghe, and Ang was transferred to the rank of Duke of Geng.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，盎來朝，太宗宴賜甚厚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan Ang came to court; Taizong feasted and rewarded him with exceptional generosity.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 5 Ang presented himself at court, and Taizong entertained and rewarded him most generously.

sentences.zh: 俄而羅竇諸洞獠叛，詔令盎率部落二萬為諸軍先鋒。

translations.literal: Soon the Liao of the Luodou and other cave districts rebelled; an edict ordered Ang to lead twenty thousand of his tribesmen as vanguard of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Liao of Luodou and the other cave districts rose in revolt; the court ordered Ang to lead twenty thousand of his tribesmen as the vanguard of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 時有賊數萬屯據險要，不可攻逼。

translations.literal: At the time tens of thousands of rebels held strategic passes and could not be pressed by attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels held the mountain passes and could not be dislodged by direct assault.

sentences.zh: 盎持弩語左右曰：「盡吾此箭，可知勝負。」

translations.literal: Ang took up his crossbow and told those beside him: "When I have spent these arrows, you will know victory or defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Ang raised his crossbow and said to his attendants, "When I have shot these arrows, you will know how the battle stands."

sentences.zh: 連發七矢，而中七人，賊退走，因縱兵乘之，斬首千余級。

translations.literal: He loosed seven bolts in succession and struck down seven men; the rebels retreated, and he unleashed his troops in pursuit, taking more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He fired seven bolts in a row and struck down seven men. The rebels broke and fled; he drove his troops after them and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 太宗令智戴還慰省之，自後賞賜不可勝數。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Zhidai back to comfort and inspect him; thereafter rewards and gifts were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Zhidai home to comfort and look after him; from then on rewards and gifts poured in without end.

sentences.zh: 盎奴婢萬余人，所居地方二千里，勤於簿領，詰擿奸狀，甚得其情。

translations.literal: Ang had more than ten thousand slaves and servants; his domain covered two thousand li. Diligent in records and accounts, he interrogated and exposed wrongdoing and grasped the facts with great precision.
translations.idiomatic: Ang kept more than ten thousand slaves and servants and ruled a domain of two thousand li. He was assiduous in paperwork, probing and exposing misconduct until he had the truth of every case.

sentences.zh: 二十年卒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twentieth year of Zhenguan.

sentences.zh: 贈左騎衛大將軍、荊州都督。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Cavalry Guard and Area Commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General-in-Chief of the Left Cavalry Guard and Area Commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 阿史那社爾，突厥處羅可汗子也。

translations.literal: Ashina She'er, son of the Türk Qaghan Chulu.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina She'er was a son of the Türk Qaghan Chulu.

sentences.zh: 年十一，以智勇稱於本蕃，拜為拓設，建牙於磧北，與欲谷設分統鐵勒、紇骨、同羅等諸部。

translations.literal: At age eleven he was famed in his tribe for wisdom and courage; he was appointed Tuo She, established his headquarters north of the desert, and with Yugu She jointly commanded the Tiele, Hegu, Tongluo, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he was already renowned in his tribe for wisdom and courage. He was made Tuo She, set up his headquarters north of the desert, and with Yugu She jointly ruled the Tiele, Hegu, Tongluo, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 在位十年，無所課斂。

translations.literal: During ten years in office he levied no exactions.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years in office he exacted no levies from his people.

sentences.zh: 諸首領或鄙其不能富貴，社爾曰：「部落既豐，於我便足。」

translations.literal: Some chieftains despised him for failing to enrich himself; She'er said: "Now that the tribes are prosperous, that is enough for me."
translations.idiomatic: Some chieftains looked down on him for not enriching himself. She'er said, "My tribes are already prosperous — that is wealth enough for me."

sentences.zh: 諸首領鹹畏而愛之。

translations.literal: All the chieftains both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains came to respect and love him alike.

sentences.zh: 武德九年，延陀、回紇等諸部皆叛，攻破欲谷設，社爾擊之，復為延陀所敗。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wude the Tiele, Uyghur, and other tribes all rebelled, overthrew Yugu She, and She'er attacked them but was again defeated by the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 9 the Tiele, Uyghurs, and other tribes all rose in revolt, overthrew Yugu She, and when She'er struck back he was defeated again by the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，遂率其余眾保於西偏，依可汗浮圖。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he led his remaining followers to shelter in the western regions, relying on the Qaghan Fotu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 2 he led his surviving followers westward and placed himself under the Qaghan Fotu.

sentences.zh: 後遇頡利滅，而西蕃葉護又死，奚利邲咄陸可汗兄弟爭國，社爾揚言降之，引兵西上，因襲破古蕃，半有其國，得眾十余萬，自稱都布可汗。

translations.literal: Later, when Jieli was destroyed and the Western Türk Yabghu also died, the brothers of Qaghan Xieli and Dudulu contended for the realm; She'er announced he would submit, led his army west, and by surprise overthrew the Western Türks, taking half their country and more than a hundred thousand followers, styling himself Qaghan Dubu.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli fell and the Western Türk Yabghu died as well, the brothers of the qaghans Xieli and Dudulu fought over the realm. She'er announced his submission, marched west, and in a surprise attack broke the Western Türks, seizing half their territory and more than a hundred thousand followers, and proclaimed himself Qaghan Dubu.

sentences.zh: 謂其諸部曰：「首為背叛破我國者，延陀之罪也。

translations.literal: He told his tribes: "The first to betray us and destroy our state was the Tiele — that is their crime.
translations.idiomatic: He told his tribes, "The Tiele were the first to betray us and destroy our state — that is their crime.

sentences.zh: 今我據有西方，大得兵馬，不平延陀而取安樂，是忘先可汗，為不孝也。

translations.literal: Now that I hold the West and have gathered great armies and horses, if I do not settle accounts with the Tiele but instead seek ease, I would forget the former qaghan and be unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I hold the West and command great armies, if I do not settle accounts with the Tiele but seek only my own comfort, I would forget the former qaghan and be unfilial.

sentences.zh: 若天令不捷，死亦無恨。」

translations.literal: If Heaven does not grant victory, I shall die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven does not grant me victory, I shall die without regret."

sentences.zh: 其酋長鹹諫曰：「今新得西方，須留鎮壓。

translations.literal: His chieftains all remonstrated: "We have only just taken the West and must remain to hold it down.
translations.idiomatic: His chieftains all urged him, "We have only just won the West and must stay to hold it.

sentences.zh: 若即棄去，遠擊延陀，只恐葉護子孫必來復國。」

translations.literal: If we abandon it now and strike the Tiele from afar, we fear the Yabghu's descendants will surely come to restore their state."
translations.idiomatic: If we leave now to attack the Tiele in the distance, the Yabghu's descendants will surely return and reclaim the realm."

sentences.zh: 社爾不從，親率五萬余騎討延陀於磧北，連兵百余日。

translations.literal: She'er would not listen and personally led more than fifty thousand horsemen to campaign against the Tiele north of the desert; fighting continued for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: She'er would not heed them. He personally led more than fifty thousand horsemen north of the desert against the Tiele, and the fighting went on for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 遇我行人劉善因立同娥設為咥利始可汗，社爾部兵又苦久役，多委之逃。

translations.literal: He encountered our envoy Liu Shanyin, who had installed Tong'e She as Qaghan Xielishi; She'er's troops, weary of long service, mostly deserted and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He ran into the Tang envoy Liu Shanyin, who had installed Tong'e She as Qaghan Xielishi. She'er's men, worn down by the long campaign, deserted in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 延陀因縱擊敗之，復保高昌國。

translations.literal: The Tiele thereupon pressed the attack and defeated him; he again took refuge in Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele pressed their attack and routed him; he fled once more to Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 其舊兵在者才萬余人，又與西蕃結隙。

translations.literal: Of his former troops only a little more than ten thousand remained, and he again fell into conflict with the Western Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Only a little more than ten thousand of his old soldiers remained, and he was again at odds with the Western Türks.

sentences.zh: 九年，率眾內屬，拜左騎衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he led his followers to submit to the interior and was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he led his people to submit to the Tang and was made General-in-Chief of the Left Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，令尚衡陽長公主，授駙馬都尉，典屯兵於苑內。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was given the Princess of Hengyang in marriage, appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and put in charge of garrison troops within the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was married to the Princess of Hengyang, appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and placed in command of garrison troops within the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授行軍總管，以平高昌。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Campaign Commander to pacify Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Campaign Commander and pacified Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 諸人鹹即受賞，社爾以未奉詔旨，秋毫無所取。

translations.literal: All the others at once accepted rewards, but She'er, having received no imperial order, took not the slightest thing.
translations.idiomatic: The others all accepted their rewards at once, but She'er had received no imperial order and took not a single thing.

sentences.zh: 及降別敕，然後受之。

translations.literal: Only when a separate edict was issued did he then accept.
translations.idiomatic: Only when a separate edict was issued did he accept anything.

sentences.zh: 及所取，唯老弱故弊而已。

translations.literal: What he took was only the old, weak, and worn-out.
translations.idiomatic: What he took was only what was old, weak, or worn out.

sentences.zh: 軍還，太宗美其廉慎，以高昌所得寶刀並雜彩千段賜之，仍令檢校北門左屯營，封畢國公。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Taizong praised his integrity and prudence, bestowing on him the precious swords taken at Gaochang together with a thousand lengths of assorted silks, and also ordered him to inspect the Left Garrison Camp at the North Gate, enfeoffing him as Duke of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Taizong praised his integrity and restraint, gave him the precious swords taken at Gaochang together with a thousand lengths of assorted silks, put him in charge of the Left Garrison Camp at the North Gate, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Bi.

sentences.zh: 十九年，從太宗征遼，至駐蹕陣，頻遭流矢，拔而又進。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he followed Taizong on the Liaodong campaign; at the Zhubi formation he was repeatedly struck by stray arrows, yet pulled them out and pressed forward.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he followed Taizong on the Liaodong campaign. At the Zhubi formation he was hit again and again by stray arrows, yet each time he pulled them out and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 其所部兵士，人百其勇，盡獲殊勛。

translations.literal: The soldiers under his command each fought with redoubled courage and all won extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers under his command fought with redoubled courage, and all won extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 師旋，兼授鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was concurrently appointed Minister of Ceremonies for Foreign Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was also made Minister of Ceremonies for Foreign Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，為昆丘道行軍大總管，征龜茲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he served as Grand Campaign Commander of the Kunqiu Route to campaign against Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made Grand Campaign Commander of the Kunqiu Route and marched against Kucha.

sentences.zh: 明年，軍次西突厥，擊處密，大破之，余眾悉降。

translations.literal: The next year the army reached the Western Türks, struck Chumi, and inflicted a great defeat; the remainder all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his army reached the Western Türks, attacked Chumi, and routed them; the survivors all submitted.

sentences.zh: 又下龜茲大撥換城，虜龜茲王白訶黎布失畢及大臣那利等百余人而還。

translations.literal: He also took the great city of Boluohuan in Kucha, captured the Kucha king Baihela Bushibi and the minister Nali together with more than a hundred others, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He also took the great city of Boluohuan in Kucha, captured the Kucha king Baihela Bushibi and the minister Nali along with more than a hundred others, and returned.

sentences.zh: 屬太宗崩，請以身殉葬，高宗遣使喻以先旨，不許。

translations.literal: When Taizong died he requested to follow him in death; Gaozong sent an envoy to explain the late emperor's intent and would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died he asked to be buried with him. Gaozong sent an envoy to explain the late emperor's wishes and refused.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，加位鎮軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 4 he was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，贈輔國大將軍、并州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; he was posthumously appointed General Who Assists the State and Area Commander of Bingzhou, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year and was posthumously made General Who Assists the State and Area Commander of Bingzhou, with the honor of burial at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 起冢以象蔥山，仍為立碑，謚曰元。

translations.literal: A tomb mound was raised in the likeness of Mount Cong, a stele was erected, and his posthumous title was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A tomb mound was raised in the shape of Mount Cong, a stele was set up, and he was given the posthumous title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子道真，位至左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Daozhen rose to General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daozhen rose to General-in-Chief of the Left Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，阿史那蘇尼失者，啟民可汗之母弟，社{人小}叔祖也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Ashina Sunishi was the younger brother of Qaghan Qimin's mother and She'er's grand-uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, Ashina Sunishi was the younger brother of Qaghan Qimin's mother and She'er's grand-uncle.

sentences.zh: 其父始畢可汗以為沙缽羅設，督部落五萬家，牙直靈州之西北，驍雄有恩惠，甚得種落之心。

translations.literal: His father, Qaghan Shibi, had made him Shaboluo She, commanding fifty thousand households of the tribes; his headquarters stood northwest of Lingzhou. Bold and generous, he won the hearts of the tribes exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qaghan Shibi had made him Shaboluo She, in charge of fifty thousand tribal households, with his headquarters northwest of Lingzhou. Bold and generous, he won the deep loyalty of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 及頡利政亂，而蘇尼失所部獨不攜離。

translations.literal: When Jieli's rule fell into disorder, Sunishi alone among those who lost their tribes did not abandon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli's rule collapsed, Sunishi alone among the dispossessed chiefs did not desert him.

sentences.zh: 突利之來奔也，頡利乃立蘇尼失為小可汗。

translations.literal: When Tuli came to surrender, Jieli thereupon installed Sunishi as Lesser Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuli came over to the Tang, Jieli installed Sunishi as Lesser Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 及頡利為李靖所破，獨騎而投之，蘇尼失遂舉其眾歸國，因令子忠擒頡利以獻。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated by Li Jing and came alone on horseback to seek refuge with him, Sunishi thereupon led all his followers to submit to the state and had his son Zhong capture Jieli and present him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing defeated Jieli and Jieli came alone on horseback to seek him out, Sunishi led all his followers to submit to the Tang and had his son Zhong capture Jieli and present him to the court.

sentences.zh: 太宗賞賜優厚。

translations.literal: Taizong rewarded him with exceptional generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rewarded him most generously.

sentences.zh: 拜北寧州都督、右衛大將軍，封懷德郡王。

translations.literal: He was appointed Area Commander of Beining Prefecture and General-in-Chief of the Right Guard, and enfeoffed as Prince of Huaide Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Area Commander of Beining, General-in-Chief of the Right Guard, and enfeoffed as Prince of Huaide Commandery.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenguan 8.

sentences.zh: 忠以擒頡利功，拜左屯衛將軍，妻以宗女定襄縣主，賜名為忠，單稱史氏。

translations.literal: For capturing Jieli, Zhong was appointed General of the Left Garrison Guard, given an imperial clanswoman, the Princess of Dingxiang County, in marriage, granted the name Zhong, and styled simply the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing Jieli, Zhong was made General of the Left Garrison Guard, married to an imperial clanswoman, the Princess of Dingxiang County, granted the name Zhong, and known simply as the Shi clan.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，遷右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 9 he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，封薛國公，累遷右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xue and successively promoted to General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xue and eventually rose to General-in-Chief of the Right Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 所歷皆以清謹見稱，時人比之金日磾。

translations.literal: In every post he was praised for integrity and prudence; men of the time compared him to Jinti.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he was praised for integrity and restraint; contemporaries compared him to Jinti.

sentences.zh: 上元初卒，贈鎮軍大將軍，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Shangyuan era; he was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Shangyuan era and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army, with the honor of burial at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 子暕，襲封薛國公，垂拱中，歷位司仆卿。

translations.literal: His son Jian inherited the fief as Duke of Xue; during the Chuigong era he served as Director of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian inherited the title Duke of Xue and during the Chuigong era served as Director of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力，其先鐵勒別部之酋長也。

translations.literal: Qibi Heli — his ancestors had been chieftains of a separate branch of the Tiele.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli — his forebears had been chieftains of a separate branch of the Tiele.

sentences.zh: 父葛，隋大業中繼為莫賀咄特勒，以地逼吐谷渾，所居隘狹，又多瘴癘，遂入龜茲，居於熱海之上。

translations.literal: His father Ge, during the Daye era of Sui, succeeded as Moheduo Tegin; because their land bordered Tuyuhun, their dwelling was cramped and narrow and malarial vapors were many, so they entered Kucha and dwelt above the Hot Sea.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ge succeeded as Moheduo Tegin during the Daye era of Sui. Their lands bordered Tuyuhun, the territory was cramped, and malarial vapors were rife, so they moved into Kucha and settled above the Hot Sea.

sentences.zh: 特勤死，何力時年九歲。

translations.literal: When the Tegin died, Heli was nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tegin died, Heli was nine years old.

sentences.zh: 降號大俟利發。

translations.literal: He was given the lesser title Great Irkin.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the lesser title Great Irkin.

sentences.zh: 至貞觀六年，隨其母率眾千余家詣沙州，奉表內附，太宗置其部落於甘、涼二州。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Zhenguan he followed his mother in leading more than a thousand households to Shazhou, submitted a memorial to submit to the interior, and Taizong settled their tribe in Gan and Liang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6 he followed his mother in leading more than a thousand households to Shazhou and submitted a memorial pledging allegiance to the Tang. Taizong settled their tribe in Gan and Liang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 何力至京，授左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Heli reached the capital he was appointed General of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Heli reached the capital he was made General of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 七年，與涼州都督李大亮、將軍薛萬均同征吐谷渾。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he campaigned against Tuyuhun together with the Area Commander of Liangzhou Li Daliang and the general Xue Wanjun.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he campaigned against Tuyuhun together with Li Daliang, Area Commander of Liangzhou, and the general Xue Wanjun.

sentences.zh: 軍次赤水川，萬均率騎先行，為賊所攻，兄弟皆中槍墮馬，徒步而鬥，兵士死者十六七。

translations.literal: When the army reached Chishui River, Wanjun led the cavalry ahead and was attacked by the enemy; both brothers were struck by spears and fell from their horses, yet fought on foot; sixty or seventy percent of the soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the Chishui River, Wanjun led the cavalry ahead and was ambushed. Both brothers were speared and thrown from their horses but fought on foot; six or seven soldiers in ten were killed.

sentences.zh: 何力聞之，將數百騎馳往，突圍而前，縱橫奮擊，賊兵披靡，萬均兄弟由是獲免。

translations.literal: When Heli heard of it he led several hundred horsemen in a gallop to the scene, broke through the encirclement and pressed forward, striking fiercely in every direction until the enemy scattered; Wanjun and his brothers were thus saved.
translations.idiomatic: When Heli heard of it he galloped forward with several hundred horsemen, broke through the encirclement, and struck fiercely in every direction until the enemy scattered. Wanjun and his brothers were thus saved.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾主在突淪川，何力復欲襲之，萬均懲其前敗，固言不可。

translations.literal: At the time the Tuyuhun ruler was at Tulun River; Heli wished again to strike him, but Wanjun, chastened by his earlier defeat, firmly said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun ruler was then at Tulun River. Heli wanted to strike again, but Wanjun, chastened by his earlier defeat, insisted it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 何力曰：「賊非有城郭，逐水草以為生，若不襲其不虞，便恐鳥驚魚散，一失機會，安可傾其巢穴耶！」

translations.literal: Heli said: "These enemies have no walled cities but live by following water and pasture. If we do not strike when they are unprepared, we fear they will scatter like startled birds and fish — once the chance is lost, how can we overturn their nest?"
translations.idiomatic: Heli said, "These enemies have no walled cities but live by following water and pasture. If we do not strike while they are unprepared, they will scatter like startled birds — and once the chance is lost, how can we overturn their nest?"

sentences.zh: 乃自選驍兵千余騎，直入突淪川，襲破吐谷渾牙帳，斬首數千級，獲駝馬牛羊二十余萬頭，渾主脫身以免，俘其妻子而還。

translations.literal: He thereupon himself selected more than a thousand elite horsemen, drove straight into Tulun River, and by surprise overthrew the Tuyuhun headquarters; several thousand heads were taken, and more than two hundred thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep were captured. The Tuyuhun ruler escaped with his life; Heli took his wife and children and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then chose more than a thousand elite horsemen himself and drove straight into Tulun River, surprising and destroying the Tuyuhun headquarters. Several thousand heads were taken and more than two hundred thousand camels, horses, cattle, and sheep captured. The Tuyuhun ruler escaped; Heli took his wife and children and returned.

sentences.zh: 有詔勞於大鬥拔谷。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that he be rewarded at Dadou Valley.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that he be rewarded at Dadou Valley.

sentences.zh: 萬均乃排毀何力，自稱己功。

translations.literal: Wanjun thereupon slandered Heli and claimed the merit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wanjun then slandered Heli and claimed the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 何力不勝憤怒，拔刀而起，欲殺萬均，諸將勸止之。

translations.literal: Heli, unable to contain his rage, drew his blade and rose to kill Wanjun; the generals urged him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Heli, unable to contain his fury, drew his blade and rose to kill Wanjun; the other generals restrained him.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而責問其故，何力言萬均敗恧之事，太宗怒，將解其官回授，何力固讓曰：「以臣之故而解萬均，恐諸蕃聞之，以為陛下厚蕃輕漢，轉相誣告，馳競必多。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it he questioned the reason; Heli spoke of Wanjun's shameful defeat. Taizong was angry and was about to strip Wanjun of his office and transfer it to Heli, but Heli firmly declined, saying: "If Wanjun is dismissed because of me, I fear the various frontier peoples will hear of it and think Your Majesty favors the tribes over the Han — they will turn to mutual slander and rivalry will surely multiply.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong heard of it he questioned the cause. Heli told of Wanjun's shameful defeat. Taizong was angry and was about to strip Wanjun of his post and give it to Heli, but Heli firmly declined. "If Wanjun is dismissed because of me," he said, "the frontier peoples will think Your Majesty favors the tribes over the Han. Mutual slander and rivalry will surely multiply.

sentences.zh: 又夷狄無知，或謂漢臣皆如此輩，固非安寧之術也。」

translations.literal: Moreover the barbarians are ignorant; some may say that all Han officials are like this — that is surely no path to peace."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the barbarians are simple-minded; some may conclude that all Han officials are like this — that is no way to secure peace."

sentences.zh: 太宗乃止。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 尋令北門宿衛，檢校屯營事，敕尚臨洮縣主。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to garrison the North Gate, placed in charge of garrison camp affairs, and commanded to marry the Princess of Lintao County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was assigned to garrison the North Gate, put in charge of the garrison camps, and commanded to marry the Princess of Lintao County.

sentences.zh: 十四年，為蔥山道副大總管，討平高昌。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he served as Deputy Grand Commander of the Congshan Route and pacified Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Deputy Grand Commander of the Congshan Route and helped pacify Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 時何力母姑臧夫人、母弟賀蘭州都督沙門並在涼府。

translations.literal: At that time Heli's mother Lady Guzang and his maternal younger brother Shamun, Area Commander of Helanzhou, were both at the Liang prefecture headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Heli's mother Lady Guzang and his maternal younger brother Shamun, Area Commander of Helanzhou, were both residing at the Liang prefecture headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔許何力觀省其母，兼撫巡部落。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict permitted Heli to visit and attend to his mother, and also to pacify and inspect the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year an edict allowed Heli to visit his mother and also charged him with pacifying and inspecting the tribes.

sentences.zh: 時薛延陀強盛，契苾部落皆願從之。

translations.literal: At the time Xueyantuo was powerful, and the Qibi tribes all wished to follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo was then at the height of its power, and the Qibi tribes all wished to join them.

sentences.zh: 何力至，聞而大驚曰：「主上於汝有厚恩，任我又重，何忍而圖叛逆！」

translations.literal: When Heli arrived, he heard of it and cried out in great alarm: "The Sovereign has shown you deep favor and entrusted me with heavy responsibility — how can you bear to plot rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: When Heli arrived and heard of it, he cried out in alarm: "The Sovereign has shown you deep favor and entrusted me with heavy responsibility — how can you bear to plot rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 諸首領皆曰：「可敦及都督已去，何故不行？」

translations.literal: All the chieftains said: "The khatun and the area commander have already gone — why should we not go?"
translations.idiomatic: All the chieftains said, "The khatun and the area commander have already gone — why should we not follow?"

sentences.zh: 何力曰：「我弟沙門孝而能養，我以身許國，終不能去也。」

translations.literal: Heli said: "My younger brother Shamun is filial and able to support our mother. I have pledged my body to the state — I can never leave."
translations.idiomatic: Heli said, "My younger brother Shamun is filial and can care for our mother. I have pledged myself to the state — I cannot leave."

sentences.zh: 於是眾共執何力至延陀所，置於可汗牙前。

translations.literal: Thereupon the multitude together seized Heli and took him to the Xueyantuo encampment, placing him before the khan's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the tribesmen seized Heli and carried him to the Xueyantuo camp, placing him before the khan's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 何力箕踞而坐，拔佩刀東向大呼曰：「豈有大唐烈士，受辱蕃庭，天地日月，願知我心！」

translations.literal: Heli sat with legs sprawled, drew his belt knife, faced east and shouted: "Can there be a stalwart of Great Tang who suffers disgrace in a barbarian court? Heaven and earth, sun and moon — may they know my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Heli sat with legs sprawled, drew his belt knife, faced east, and shouted: "Can a stalwart of Great Tang suffer disgrace in a barbarian court? Heaven and earth, sun and moon — let them know my heart!"

sentences.zh: 又割左耳以明誌不奪也。

translations.literal: He then cut off his left ear to show that his resolve could not be taken from him.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut off his left ear to show that his resolve could not be broken.

sentences.zh: 可汗怒，欲殺之，為其妻所抑而止。

translations.literal: The khan was angered and wished to kill him, but was restrained and stopped by his wife.
translations.idiomatic: The khan was enraged and wanted to kill him, but his wife restrained him and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗聞何力之延陀，明非其本意。

translations.literal: Initially, when Taizong heard that Heli had gone to Xueyantuo, he understood clearly that it was not his true intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong first heard that Heli had gone over to Xueyantuo, he understood at once that it was not Heli's true intent.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「人心各樂其土，何力今入延陀，猶魚之得水也。」

translations.literal: Some said: "Every man's heart delights in his native soil; now that Heli has entered Xueyantuo, it is like a fish finding water."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "Every man delights in his native land; now that Heli has joined Xueyantuo, it is like a fish returned to water."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「不然，此人心如鐵石，必不背我。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Not so — this man's heart is like iron and stone; he will surely not betray me."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Not so. This man's heart is iron and stone; he will never betray me."

sentences.zh: 會有使自延陀至，具言其狀，太守泣謂群臣曰：「契苾何力竟如何？」

translations.literal: Just then an envoy arrived from Xueyantuo and reported the whole affair in detail. Taizong wept and said to his ministers: "What has become of Qibi Heli?"
translations.idiomatic: Just then an envoy arrived from Xueyantuo and reported everything in detail. Taizong wept and said to his ministers, "What has become of Qibi Heli?"

sentences.zh: 遽遣兵部侍郎崔敦禮持節入延陀，許降公主，求何力。

translations.literal: He immediately dispatched Vice Minister of War Cui Dunli bearing credentials into Xueyantuo, promising a princess in marriage and demanding Heli's return.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent Vice Minister of War Cui Dunli with imperial credentials into Xueyantuo, promising a princess in marriage in exchange for Heli's return.

sentences.zh: 由是還，拜右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Thereby Heli returned and was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Heli was thus returned and appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗既許公主於延陀，行有日矣，何力抗表固言不可。

translations.literal: Taizong having already promised a princess to Xueyantuo and the day of departure drawing near, Heli submitted a memorial firmly stating that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had already promised a princess to Xueyantuo and the wedding day was near when Heli submitted a memorial firmly urging against it.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「吾聞天子無戲言，既已許之，安可廢？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "I have heard that a Son of Heaven does not speak in jest — having already promised, how can it be revoked?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I have heard that a Son of Heaven does not speak in jest. Having already promised, how can the pledge be withdrawn?"

sentences.zh: 何力曰：「然。

translations.literal: Heli said: "Indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Heli said, "Indeed.

sentences.zh: 臣本請延緩其事，不謂總停。

translations.literal: Your subject originally asked only to delay the matter — I did not mean to stop it altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject originally asked only to delay the matter; I did not mean to cancel it entirely.

sentences.zh: 臣聞六禮之內，婿合親迎，宜告延陀親來迎婦，縱不敢至京邑，即當使詣靈州。

translations.literal: I have heard that among the six rites of marriage the groom must personally come to welcome the bride. We should tell Xueyantuo to come in person to fetch his bride — even if he dares not come to the capital, he should at least be sent to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that among the six rites of marriage the groom must come in person to welcome the bride. Tell Xueyantuo to fetch his bride himself — and even if he dares not come to the capital, require him to come at least as far as Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 畏漢必不敢來，論親未可有成日。

translations.literal: Fearing the Han he will surely not come — and with the betrothal unsettled, no date for the union can be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Tang he will surely not come, and with the betrothal unsettled no wedding day can be fixed.

sentences.zh: 既憂悶，臣又攜離，不盈一年，自相猜忌。

translations.literal: With worry and vexation on both sides and your subject also taken away from them, within less than a year they will suspect one another.
translations.idiomatic: With vexation on both sides and your subject also removed from them, within a year they will turn suspicious of one another.

sentences.zh: 延陀誌性狠戾，若死，必兩子相爭，坐而制之，必然之理。」

translations.literal: Xueyantuo is by nature fierce and harsh; when he dies his two sons will surely contend — to control them while seated at ease is the inevitable outcome."
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo is fierce and harsh by nature. When he dies his two sons will surely fight over power — and we can control them without stirring from our seats. That is inevitable."

sentences.zh: 太宗從之。

translations.literal: Taizong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 延陀恐有詐，竟不至靈州。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo, fearing a trap, in the end did not come to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo, fearing treachery, in the end never came to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 自後常悒悒不得誌，一年而死，兩子果爭權，各立為主。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was constantly dejected and unable to achieve his aim; within a year he died, and the two sons indeed fought over power, each setting himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he remained dejected and frustrated; within a year he died, and the two sons did indeed fight for power, each proclaiming himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼東，以何力為前軍總管，軍次白崖城，為賊所圍，被矛中腰，瘡重疾甚，太宗自為傅藥。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, Heli was made Vanguard Commander. When the army halted at Baiya City he was surrounded by the enemy, struck in the waist by a spear, and his wound was grave and severe — Taizong personally applied medicine for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, Heli served as Vanguard Commander. At Baiya City the army was surrounded; Heli was speared in the waist and his wound was grave. Taizong personally dressed it for him.

sentences.zh: 及拔賊城，敕求傷之者高突勃，付何力自殺之。

translations.literal: When the enemy city was taken, an edict sought out Gao Tublue, who had wounded him, and handed him over to Heli to kill.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy city was taken, an edict sought out Gao Tublue, the man who had wounded him, and handed him over to Heli to execute.

sentences.zh: 何力奏言：「犬馬猶為其主，況於人乎？

translations.literal: Heli memorialized: "Even dogs and horses serve their masters — how much more so men?
translations.idiomatic: Heli memorialized, "Even dogs and horses serve their masters — how much more so men?

sentences.zh: 彼為其主，況致命冒白刃而刺臣，是其義勇士也。

translations.literal: He acted for his lord, and moreover risked his life and braved bare blades to spear me — that is a righteous brave man.
translations.idiomatic: He acted for his lord, and moreover risked his life and braved naked steel to spear me — that is a righteous warrior.

sentences.zh: 本不相識，豈是冤仇？」

translations.literal: We were strangers to begin with — how could this be a private feud?"
translations.idiomatic: We were strangers to begin with — how could this be a personal vendetta?"

sentences.zh: 遂舍之。

translations.literal: He thereupon released him.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon released him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，為昆丘道總管，擊龜茲，獲其王訶梨布失畢及諸首領等。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as Commander of the Kunqiu Route, attacked Kucha, and captured its king Helibushibi and various chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made Commander of the Kunqiu Route, attacked Kucha, and captured its king Helibushibi along with various chieftains.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，何力欲殺身以殉，高宗諭而止之。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Heli wished to kill himself to follow him in death; Gaozong admonished him and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, Heli wished to take his own life in sacrifice; Gaozong admonished him and forbade it.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，處月、處密叛，以何力為弓月道大總管，討平之，擒其渠帥處密時健俟斤、合支賀等以歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, Chuyue and Chumi rebelled. Heli was made Grand Commander of the Gongyue Route, pacified them, and captured their leaders Chumi Shijian Irkin, Hezhih, and others and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 2 the Chuyue and Chumi rebelled. Heli was made Grand Commander of the Gongyue Route, suppressed them, and captured their chieftains Chumi Shijian Irkin, Hezhih, and others.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，遷左驍衛大將軍，累封郕國公，兼檢校鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Bi, and concurrently made Acting Minister of Reception.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 he was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Bi, and concurrently appointed Acting Minister of Reception.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，又為遼東道行軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo he again served as Grand Commander of the Liaodong Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 1 he was again made Grand Commander of the Liaodong Campaign.

sentences.zh: 九月，次於鴨綠水，其地即高麗之險阻，莫離支男生以精兵數萬守之，眾莫能濟。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army halted at the Yalu River — a strategic strongpoint of Goguryeo. Molizhi Nansheng guarded it with tens of thousands of elite troops, and none could cross.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army halted at the Yalu River, a strategic strongpoint of Goguryeo. Molizhi Nansheng held it with tens of thousands of elite troops, and none could cross.

sentences.zh: 何力始至，會層冰大合，趣即渡兵，鼓噪而進，賊遂大潰，追奔數十里，斬首三萬級，余眾盡降，男生僅以身免。

translations.literal: When Heli first arrived, thick ice had frozen over in layers. He hurried to ferry troops across, advanced with drums and battle cries, and the enemy was routed. They pursued the fleeing foe for several tens of li, cut off thirty thousand heads, the remainder all surrendered, and Nansheng barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Heli arrived, thick ice had formed in layers. He hurried troops across the river, advanced with drums and shouts, and the enemy broke and fled. The pursuit ran for several tens of li; thirty thousand heads were taken, the rest surrendered, and Nansheng barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 會有詔班師，乃還。

translations.literal: Just then an edict ordered withdrawal, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Just then an edict ordered withdrawal, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 其年，九姓叛，以何力為鐵勒道安撫大使。

translations.literal: That same year the Nine Surnames rebelled, and Heli was made Pacification Commissioner of the Tiele Route.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Nine Surnames rebelled, and Heli was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Tiele Route.

sentences.zh: 乃簡精騎五百馳入九姓中，賊大驚，何力乃謂曰：「國家知汝被詿誤，遂有翻動，使我舍汝等過，皆可自新。

translations.literal: He selected five hundred elite horsemen and galloped into the midst of the Nine Surnames. The rebels were greatly alarmed. Heli addressed them: "The state knows you were deceived and stirred to revolt. I am sent to pass you by in mercy — all may renew yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: He chose five hundred elite horsemen and galloped into the heart of the Nine Surnames. The rebels were terrified. Heli told them, "The state knows you were misled into revolt. I am sent to pass you by in mercy — all of you may start anew.

sentences.zh: 罪在酋渠，得之則已。」

translations.literal: Guilt lies with the tribal leaders — once they are seized, that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Guilt rests with the tribal leaders; once they are taken, that is enough."

sentences.zh: 諸姓大喜，共擒偽葉護及設、特勤等同惡二百余人以歸，何力數其罪而誅之。

translations.literal: All the tribes rejoiced greatly. Together they seized the false yabgu and more than two hundred co-conspirators including she and tegin and returned with them. Heli enumerated their crimes and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes rejoiced and together seized the false yabgu and more than two hundred co-conspirators, including she and tegin, and handed them over. Heli listed their crimes and executed them.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，又為遼東道行軍大總管，兼安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng he again served as Grand Commander of the Liaodong Campaign, concurrently Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfeng 1 he was again made Grand Commander of the Liaodong Campaign and concurrently Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 高麗有眾十五萬，屯於遼水，又引靺鞨數萬據南蘇城。

translations.literal: Goguryeo had a force of one hundred fifty thousand encamped at the Liao River, and also brought in tens of thousands of Mohe to hold Nansu City.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo had one hundred fifty thousand troops encamped at the Liao River and also brought in tens of thousands of Mohe to hold Nansu City.

sentences.zh: 何力奮擊，皆大破之。

translations.literal: Heli struck fiercely and routed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Heli struck fiercely and routed them all.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬余級，乘勝而進，凡拔七城。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand heads were cut. Pressing the advantage forward, seven cities in all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand heads were taken. Pressing the advantage, he captured seven cities in all.

sentences.zh: 乃回軍會英國公李勣於鴨綠水，共攻辱夷、大行二城，破之。

translations.literal: He then turned his army and joined the Duke of Ying Li Ji at the Yalu River, jointly attacking the cities of Ruyi and Daxing and taking them.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned back and joined the Duke of Ying, Li Ji, at the Yalu River. Together they attacked the cities of Ruyi and Daxing and captured them.

sentences.zh: 勣頓軍於鴨綠柵，何力引蕃漢兵五十萬先臨平壤。

translations.literal: Ji halted his army at the Yalu stockade. Heli led five hundred thousand tribal and Han troops to advance first on Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji halted his army at the Yalu stockade while Heli led five hundred thousand tribal and Han troops to advance first on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 勣仍繼至，共拔平壤城，執男建，虜其王還。

translations.literal: Ji followed after, and together they took Pyongyang, captured Namgeon, and carried off the king in captivity.
translations.idiomatic: Ji followed after, and together they captured Pyongyang, seized Namgeon, and carried off the king.

sentences.zh: 授鎮軍大將軍，行左衛大將軍，徙封涼國公，仍檢校右羽林軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, acting General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liang, and he remained Acting Commander of the Right Forest Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and acting General-in-Chief of the Left Guard, his title was changed to Duke of Liang, and he remained Acting Commander of the Right Forest Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年卒，贈輔國大將軍、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰烈。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng he died. He was posthumously honored as General Who Assists the State and Area Commander of Bingzhou, buried with honors at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous name Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yifeng 2. Posthumously he was honored as General Who Assists the State and Area Commander of Bingzhou, buried with honors at Zhaoling, with the posthumous name Lie.

sentences.zh: 有三子：明、光、貞。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Ming, Guang, and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Ming, Guang, and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 明，左鷹揚衛大將軍，兼賀蘭都督，襲爵涼國公。

translations.literal: Ming served as General-in-Chief of the Left Hawk Yang Guard, concurrently Area Commander of Helan, and inherited the dukedom of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ming was General-in-Chief of the Left Hawk Yang Guard and concurrently Area Commander of Helan; he inherited the dukedom of Liang.

sentences.zh: 光，則天時右豹韜衛將軍，為酷吏所殺。

translations.literal: Guang, during Wu Zetian's reign, was General of the Right Leopard Guard and was killed by cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Guang served under Wu Zetian as General of the Right Leopard Guard and was killed by cruel officials.

sentences.zh: 貞，司膳少卿。

translations.literal: Zhen was Vice Director of the Commissariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was Vice Director of the Commissariat.

sentences.zh: 黑齒常之，百濟西部人。

translations.literal: Heichi Changzhi was a native of western Baekje.
translations.idiomatic: Heichi Changzhi was a native of western Baekje.

sentences.zh: 長七尺余，驍勇有謀略。

translations.literal: Over seven feet tall, fierce and brave, with stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He stood over seven feet tall, fierce and brave, and skilled in strategy.

sentences.zh: 初在本蕃，仕為達率兼郡將，猶中國之刺史也。

translations.literal: Initially in his native state he served as Daeshu and concurrently Junjiang — equivalent to a Chinese prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In his native kingdom he had served as Daeshu and concurrently as Junjiang — the equivalent of a Chinese prefect.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，蘇定方討平百濟，常之率所部隨例送降款。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing, Su Dingfang pacified Baekje. Changzhi led his command in the usual submission of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 5 Su Dingfang pacified Baekje. Changzhi led his followers in the customary submission of surrender.

sentences.zh: 時定方縶左王及太子隆等，仍縱兵劫掠，丁壯者多被戮。

translations.literal: At the time Dingfang bound the Left King and Crown Prince Rong and others, yet let his troops plunder; able-bodied men were mostly slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang bound the Left King, Crown Prince Rong, and others, yet let his troops plunder freely. Able-bodied men were slaughtered in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 常之恐懼，遂與左右十余人遁歸本部，鳩集亡逸，共保任存山，築柵以自固，旬日而歸附者三萬余人。

translations.literal: Changzhi was terrified. With a dozen or so followers he fled back to his territory, gathered scattered refugees, together held Mount Imseok, built stockades for defense, and within ten days more than thirty thousand attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Changzhi fled with a dozen followers back to his territory, gathered scattered refugees, and together they held Mount Imseok and built stockades to defend themselves. Within ten days more than thirty thousand had joined him.

sentences.zh: 定方遣兵攻之，常之領敢死之士拒戰，官軍敗績，遂復本國二百余城，定方不能討而還。

translations.literal: Dingfang sent troops to attack. Changzhi led death-defying warriors to resist. The government army was defeated, and he recovered more than two hundred cities of the native state. Dingfang could not subdue him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang sent troops against him, but Changzhi led death-defying warriors to resist and routed the government army. He recovered more than two hundred cities of the kingdom, and Dingfang could not subdue him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，高宗遣使招諭之，常之盡率其眾降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longshuo, Gaozong sent envoys to summon and persuade him, and Changzhi led his entire following in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 3 Gaozong sent envoys to summon him, and Changzhi led his entire following in submission.

sentences.zh: 累轉左領軍員外將軍。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Outside General of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to Outside General of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，吐蕃犯邊，常之從李敬玄擊之。

translations.literal: During Yifeng, Tibet invaded the frontier. Changzhi followed Li Jingxuan to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era Tibet invaded the frontier, and Changzhi followed Li Jingxuan to repel them.

sentences.zh: 劉審禮之沒賊，敬玄欲抽軍，卻阻泥溝，而計無所出。

translations.literal: When Liu Shenli was captured by the enemy, Jingxuan wished to withdraw the army but was blocked at the muddy ravine with no plan at hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shenli fell into enemy hands, Jingxuan wanted to withdraw but was blocked at a muddy ravine and could find no way out.

sentences.zh: 常之夜率敢死之兵五百人進掩賊營，吐蕃首領跋地設棄軍宵遁，敬玄因此得還。

translations.literal: Changzhi by night led five hundred death-defying troops in a surprise raid on the enemy camp. The Tibetan leader Bodhishe abandoned his army and fled by night, and Jingxuan thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi led five hundred death-defying troops in a night raid on the enemy camp. The Tibetan leader Bodhishe abandoned his army and fled under cover of darkness, and Jingxuan was thus able to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘆其才略，擢授左武衛將軍，兼檢校左羽林軍，賜金五百兩、絹五百匹，仍充河源軍副使。

translations.literal: Gaozong admired his talent and strategy, promoted him to General of the Left Martial Guard, concurrently Acting Commander of the Left Forest Guard, granted five hundred taels of gold and five hundred bolts of silk, and appointed him Deputy Commander of the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong admired his talent and promoted him to General of the Left Martial Guard and Acting Commander of the Left Forest Guard, granted him five hundred taels of gold and five hundred bolts of silk, and made him Deputy Commander of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃贊婆及素和貴等賊徒三萬余屯於良非川。

translations.literal: At the time the Tibetan bandits Zanpo and Suhegui and others, more than thirty thousand, encamped at Liangfei River.
translations.idiomatic: At the time more than thirty thousand Tibetan raiders under Zanpo and Suhegui were encamped at the Liangfei River.

sentences.zh: 常之率精騎三千夜襲賊營，殺獲二千級，獲羊馬數萬，贊婆等單騎而遁。

translations.literal: Changzhi led three thousand elite horsemen in a night raid on the enemy camp, killed and captured two thousand, seized tens of thousands of sheep and horses, and Zanpo and the others fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi led three thousand elite horsemen in a night raid, killed and captured two thousand, seized tens of thousands of sheep and horses, and Zanpo and the others fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 擢常之為大使，又賞物四百匹。

translations.literal: Changzhi was elevated to commissioner and rewarded with four hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi was promoted to commissioner and rewarded with four hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 常之以河源軍正當賊沖，欲加兵鎮守，恐有運轉之費，遂遠置烽戍七十余所，度開營田五千余頃，歲收百余萬石。

translations.literal: Changzhi, since the Heyuan Army lay directly in the enemy's path and he wished to add garrison troops but feared transport costs, therefore established watch-beacons and outposts at more than seventy distant posts, opened more than five thousand qing of garrison farms, and harvested more than a million shi annually.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Heyuan Army lay directly in the enemy's path, Changzhi wanted to strengthen the garrison but feared the cost of supply. He therefore established more than seventy distant beacon towers and outposts, opened more than five thousand qing of garrison farms, and harvested more than a million shi of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 開耀中，贊婆等屯於青海，常之率精兵一萬騎襲破之，燒其糧貯而還。

translations.literal: During Kaiyao, Zanpo and others encamped at Qinghai Lake. Changzhi led ten thousand elite cavalry in a raid, burned their grain stores, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyao era Zanpo and others encamped at Qinghai Lake. Changzhi led ten thousand elite cavalry in a raid, burned their grain stores, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 常之在軍七年，吐蕃深畏憚之，不敢復為邊患。

translations.literal: Changzhi was in the army seven years. Tibet deeply feared him and did not again become a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi served in the army for seven years. Tibet deeply feared him and did not again threaten the frontier.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，遷左武衛大將軍，仍檢校左羽林軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sisheng he was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard, still Acting Commander of the Left Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sisheng he was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard and remained Acting Commander of the Left Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 垂拱二年，突厥犯邊，命常之率兵拒之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong, the Turks invaded the frontier, and Changzhi was ordered to lead troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong 2 the Turks invaded the frontier, and Changzhi was ordered to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 躡至兩井，忽逢賊三千余眾，常之見賊徒爭下馬著甲，遂領二百余騎，身當先鋒直沖，賊遂棄甲而散。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Liangjing, he suddenly encountered more than three thousand enemy. Changzhi saw the bandits scrambling to dismount and don armor. He led more than two hundred horsemen, himself taking point as vanguard in a direct charge, and the enemy cast off their armor and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing as far as Liangjing, he suddenly encountered more than three thousand enemy. Seeing them scramble to dismount and don armor, Changzhi led more than two hundred horsemen and charged at the head of the vanguard. The enemy cast off their armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，賊眾大至。

translations.literal: In a moment the enemy forces arrived in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the enemy arrived in force.

sentences.zh: 及日將暮，常之令伐木，營中燃火如烽燧，時東南忽有大風起，賊疑有救兵相應，遂狼狽夜遁。

translations.literal: As dusk approached, Changzhi ordered trees felled and fires lit in camp like beacon towers. Suddenly a great wind rose from the southeast. The enemy suspected reinforcing troops and fled in disorder by night.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk fell, Changzhi ordered trees cut and fires lit in camp like beacon towers. A sudden strong wind rose from the southeast. The enemy suspected reinforcements and fled in disorder under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 以功進封燕國公。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 三年，突厥入寇朔州，常之又充大總管，以李多祚、王九言為副。

translations.literal: In the third year the Turks invaded Shuozhou. Changzhi again served as Grand Commander, with Li Duozuo and Wang Jiuyan as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Turks invaded Shuozhou. Changzhi again served as Grand Commander, with Li Duozuo and Wang Jiuyan as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 追躡至黃花堆，大破之，追奔四十餘里，賊散走磧北。

translations.literal: He pursued to Huanghuadui and routed them thoroughly, pursuing the fleeing foe for more than forty li until the bandits scattered north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them to Huanghuadui and routed them, chasing the fleeing enemy for more than forty li until they scattered north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 時有中郎將爨寶璧表請窮追余賊，制常之與寶璧會，遙為聲援。

translations.literal: At the time Middle General Cuan Baobi memorialized requesting to pursue the remaining bandits to the end. An edict ordered Changzhi and Baobi to rendezvous and provide distant support.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Middle General Cuan Baobi memorialized asking to pursue the remaining enemy to the end. An edict ordered Changzhi and Baobi to join forces and provide distant support.

sentences.zh: 寶璧以為破賊在朝夕，貪功先行，竟不與常之謀議，遂全軍而沒。

translations.literal: Baobi thought victory was a matter of days, greedily sought merit and advanced first, did not consult with Changzhi at all, and his entire army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Baobi thought victory was only days away, greedily sought glory, and advanced without consulting Changzhi at all. His entire army was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 尋為周興等誣構，雲與右鷹揚將軍趙懷節等謀反繫獄，遂自縊而死。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was falsely incriminated by Zhou Xing and others, accused of plotting rebellion with Right Hawk Yang General Zhao Huaijie and others, imprisoned, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was falsely accused by Zhou Xing and others of plotting rebellion with Right Hawk Yang General Zhao Huaijie and others. Imprisoned, he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 常之嘗有所乘馬為兵士所損，副使牛師獎等請鞭之。

translations.literal: Changzhi once had a horse he rode damaged by a soldier. Deputy Commander Niu Shijiang and others asked to flog him.
translations.idiomatic: Once a soldier damaged a horse Changzhi was riding. Deputy Commander Niu Shijiang and others asked to have him flogged.

sentences.zh: 常之曰：「豈可以損私馬而決官兵乎！」

translations.literal: Changzhi said: "How can I punish a soldier for damaging my private horse!"
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi said, "How can I punish a soldier for damaging my private horse!"

sentences.zh: 竟赦之。

translations.literal: He ultimately pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 前後所得賞賜金帛等，皆分給將士；

translations.literal: Gold, silk, and other rewards received before and after were all distributed among officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: All the gold, silk, and other rewards he received, before and after, he distributed among his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 及死，時甚惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, the age greatly mourned his loss.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the court deeply mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 李多祚，代為靺鞨酋長。

translations.literal: Li Duozuo — for generations his clan had been chieftains of the Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Duozuo — for generations his clan had served as chieftains of the Mohe.

sentences.zh: 多祚驍勇善射，意氣感激。

translations.literal: Duozuo was fierce and brave, skilled at archery, and spirited and impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo was fierce and brave, skilled at archery, and full of martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 少以軍功歷位右羽林軍大將軍，前後掌禁兵，北門宿衛二十余年。

translations.literal: From youth through military merit he rose to General-in-Chief of the Right Forest Guard; successively commanded the imperial guard and garrisoned the North Gate for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he rose through military merit to General-in-Chief of the Right Forest Guard. He successively commanded the imperial guard and garrisoned the North Gate for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，張柬之將誅張易之兄弟，引多祚將籌其事，謂曰：「將軍在北門幾年？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Zhang Jianzhi was about to execute the Zhang Yizhi brothers. He enlisted Duozuo to plan the affair and said: "General, how many years have you garrisoned the North Gate?"
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, Zhang Jianzhi was preparing to execute the Zhang Yizhi brothers. He enlisted Duozuo to help plan the affair and asked, "General, how many years have you garrisoned the North Gate?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「三十年矣。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Thirty years."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Thirty years."

sentences.zh: 柬之曰：「將軍擊鐘鼎食，金章紫綬，貴寵當代，位極武臣，豈非大帝之恩乎？」

translations.literal: Zhang said: "General, you feast from bell and tripod, bear golden seal and purple cord — honored and favored beyond your peers, risen to the pinnacle of military men — is this not the late emperor's grace?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said, "General, you feast from bell and tripod, wear golden seal and purple cord — honored and favored beyond your peers, risen to the summit of military men — is this not the late emperor's grace?"

translations.literal: He replied: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「將軍既感大帝殊澤，能有報乎？

translations.literal: He also said: "General, having felt the late emperor's special grace, can you repay it?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "General, having felt the late emperor's special grace, can you repay it?

sentences.zh: 大帝之子見在東宮，逆豎張易之兄弟擅權，朝夕危逼。

translations.literal: The late emperor's son is now in the Eastern Palace; the treacherous villains Zhang Yizhi and his brothers monopolize power, pressing danger day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's son is now in the Eastern Palace, while the treacherous Zhang Yizhi brothers monopolize power and press their threat day and night.

sentences.zh: 宗社之重，於將軍，誠能報恩，正屬今日。」

translations.literal: The weight of altar and state rests upon the general — if you can truly repay the grace, today is precisely the day."
translations.idiomatic: The fate of altar and state rests with you, General — if you can truly repay that grace, today is the day."

sentences.zh: 多祚曰：「茍緣王室，惟相公所使，終不顧妻子性命。」

translations.literal: Duozuo said: "If it serves the royal house, I shall follow wherever the Chancellor sends me, never caring for wife and children's lives."
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo said, "If it serves the royal house, I shall go wherever the Chancellor sends me, never sparing my wife and children."

sentences.zh: 因即引天地神祗為要誓，詞氣感動，義形於色。

translations.literal: Thereupon he invoked Heaven and Earth and the spirits as witnesses to a sworn pledge; his words moved all who heard, and righteousness showed in his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he invoked Heaven and Earth and the spirits as witnesses to a sworn pledge. His words moved all who heard, and righteousness showed plainly in his face.

sentences.zh: 遂與柬之等定謀誅易之兄弟，以功進封遼陽郡王，食實封八百戶，仍拜其子承訓為衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: He then joined Jianzhi and the others in plotting to execute the Yizhi brothers. For his merit he was advanced to Prince of Liaoyang Commandery with eight hundred actual fief households; his son Chengxun was also appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Guardians.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Jianzhi and the others in plotting to execute the Yizhi brothers. For his merit he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoyang Commandery with eight hundred actual fief households, and his son Chengxun was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Guardians.

sentences.zh: 其年，將有事於太廟，特令多祚與安國相王登輦夾侍。

translations.literal: That year, when rites were to be held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Duozuo was specially ordered to mount the imperial carriage alongside the Prince of An State as attendants flanking the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when rites were to be held at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Duozuo was specially ordered to mount the imperial carriage alongside the Prince of An State as attendants flanking the emperor.

sentences.zh: 監察御史王覿上疏諫曰：「竊惟祔廟之禮，在於尊祖奉先；

translations.literal: Censor Wang Di memorialized in remonstrance: "I respectfully consider that the rite of enshrining in the ancestral temple lies in honoring ancestors and serving the forefathers;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Di memorialized in remonstrance: "I respectfully consider that the rite of enshrining in the ancestral temple lies in honoring ancestors and serving the forefathers;

sentences.zh: 肅事之儀，豈厭惟親與德。

translations.literal: the solemn ceremony — does it not value kinship and virtue alone?
translations.idiomatic: the solemn ceremony — does it not value kinship and virtue alone?

sentences.zh: 伏見恩敕令安國相王與李多祚參乘，且多祚夷人，有功於國，適可加之寵爵，豈宜逼奉至尊，侍帝弟而連衡，與吾君而共輦？

translations.literal: I see that the gracious edict orders the Prince of An State and Li Duozuo to ride as companions. Moreover, Duozuo is a barbarian who has merit for the state — he may suitably receive honored titles and ranks. How can he be compelled to attend the Son of Heaven, stand beside the emperor's brother in paired rank, and share the carriage with our sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: I see that the gracious edict orders the Prince of An State and Li Duozuo to ride as companions. Duozuo is a barbarian who has served the state with merit — he may suitably receive honored titles and ranks. How can he be compelled to attend the Son of Heaven, stand beside the emperor's brother as an equal, and share the carriage with our sovereign?

sentences.zh: 誠恐萬方之人，不允所望。

translations.literal: I truly fear the people of all lands will not approve as hoped.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear the people of all lands will not approve as hoped.

sentences.zh: 昔文帝引趙談參乘，盎伏車前曰：『臣聞天子所共六尺輿者，皆天下豪英。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Wen had Zhao Tan ride as companion. Yuan Ang prostrated himself before the carriage and said: 'I have heard that those who share the Son of Heaven's six-foot carriage are all heroes of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Wen had Zhao Tan ride as companion. Yuan Ang prostrated himself before the carriage and said, 'I have heard that those who share the Son of Heaven's six-foot carriage are all heroes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今漢雖乏人，陛下獨奈何與刀鋸之余共載！』

translations.literal: Now though Han lacks men, how can Your Majesty alone ride with the dregs of executioners!'
translations.idiomatic: Now though Han lacks men, how can Your Majesty alone ride with the dregs of executioners!'

sentences.zh: 於是斥而下之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao Tan was driven off and removed from the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhao Tan was driven off and removed from the carriage.

sentences.zh: 多祚雖無趙談之累，亦非卿相之重，不自循省，無聞固讓，豈國乏良輔，更無其人。

translations.literal: Duozuo, though free of Zhao Tan's fault, is also not of ministerial or chancellor rank. Without examining himself, without the firm refusal one would expect — does the state lack worthy aides that no other man can be found?
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo, though free of Zhao Tan's fault, is also not of ministerial or chancellor rank. Without examining himself, without the firm refusal one would expect — does the state lack worthy aides that no other man can be found?

sentences.zh: 史官所書，將示於後。

translations.literal: What the historians record will be shown to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: What the historians record will be shown to posterity.

sentences.zh: 何袁盎之強諫，獨微臣之不及。

translations.literal: Why was Yuan Ang's forceful remonstrance honored while I alone fall short?
translations.idiomatic: Why was Yuan Ang's forceful remonstrance honored while I alone fall short?

sentences.zh: 惟陛下詳擇焉。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty consider carefully."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty consider carefully."

sentences.zh: 上謂覿曰：「多祚雖是夷人，緣其有功，委以心腹，特令侍輦，卿勿復言也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wang Di: "Though Duozuo is a barbarian, because of his merit I have entrusted him as one close at heart and specially ordered him to attend the carriage. Speak no more of it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wang Di, "Though Duozuo is a barbarian, because of his merit I have entrusted him as one close at heart and specially ordered him to attend the carriage. Speak no more of it."

sentences.zh: 節湣太子之殺武三思也，多祚與羽林大將軍李千里等率兵以從。

translations.literal: When the Jiemin Crown Prince killed Wu Sansi, Duozuo joined General-in-Chief of the Feathered Forest Li Qianli and others in leading troops to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiemin Crown Prince killed Wu Sansi, Duozuo joined General-in-Chief of the Feathered Forest Li Qianli and others in leading troops to follow him.

sentences.zh: 太子令多祚先至玄武樓下，冀上問以殺三思之意，遂按兵不戰。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince ordered Duozuo to advance first to below the Xuanwu Tower, hoping the emperor would question him about the intent behind Sansi's killing, and therefore held the troops at rest without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince ordered Duozuo to advance first to below the Xuanwu Tower, hoping the emperor would question him about the intent behind Sansi's killing, and therefore held the troops at rest without fighting.

sentences.zh: 時有宮闈令楊思勖於樓上侍帝，請拒其先鋒。

translations.literal: At the time Palace Ward Chief Yang Sixun was attending the emperor on the tower and requested to repel the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Palace Ward Chief Yang Sixun was attending the emperor on the tower and requested permission to repel the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 多祚子婿羽林中郎將野呼利為先軍總管，思勖挺刃斬之，兵眾大沮。

translations.literal: Duozuo's son-in-law, Captain of the Feathered Forest Yehuli, was vanguard commander. Sixun drew his blade and cut him down, and the army's morale collapsed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo's son-in-law, Captain of the Feathered Forest Yehuli, was vanguard commander. Sixun drew his blade and cut him down, and the army's morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 多祚俄為左右所殺，並殺其二子，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Before long Duozuo was killed by those at the emperor's side; both his sons were also killed, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Duozuo was killed by those at the emperor's side. Both his sons were also killed, and his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，下制曰：「以忠報國，典冊所稱；

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, he issued an edict: "Serving the state with loyalty is what the canonical records praise;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, he issued an edict: "Serving the state with loyalty is what the canonical records praise;

sentences.zh: 感義捐軀，名節斯在。

translations.literal: moved by righteousness to give one's body — integrity and reputation lie therein.
translations.idiomatic: moved by righteousness to give one's body — integrity and reputation lie therein.

sentences.zh: 故右羽林大將軍、上柱國、遼陽郡王李多祚，三韓貴種，百戰余雄。

translations.literal: The late General-in-Chief of the Right Forest Guard, Supreme Pillar of State, Prince of Liaoyang Commandery Li Duozuo — noble stock of the Three Han, a veteran hero of a hundred battles.
translations.idiomatic: The late General-in-Chief of the Right Forest Guard, Supreme Pillar of State, Prince of Liaoyang Commandery Li Duozuo — noble stock of the Three Han, a veteran hero of a hundred battles.

sentences.zh: 席寵禁營，乃心王室，仗茲誠信，翻陷誅夷。

translations.literal: He enjoyed favor in the forbidden camp, his heart devoted to the royal house; relying on this sincerity and trust, he was turned instead to execution and extermination.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed favor in the forbidden camp and his heart was devoted to the royal house, yet relying on this sincerity and trust he was turned instead to execution and extermination.

sentences.zh: 賴彼神明，重清奸慝，永言徽烈，深合褒崇。

translations.literal: Thanks to the divine spirits, treachery was again cleared away. His noble merit deserves deep commendation.
