translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the divine spirits, treachery was again cleared away. His noble merit deserves deep commendation.

sentences.zh: 宜追歿後之榮，以復生前之命。

translations.literal: He should receive posthumous honor to restore the appointment he held in life.
translations.idiomatic: He should receive posthumous honor to restore the appointment he held in life.

sentences.zh: 可還舊官，仍宥其妻子。」

translations.literal: Let his former office be restored, and let his wife and children be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Let his former office be restored, and let his wife and children be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 李嗣業，京兆高陵人也。

translations.literal: Li Siye — native of Gaoling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye was a native of Gaoling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺，壯勇絕倫。

translations.literal: Seven feet in height, unmatched in strength and courage.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall and was unmatched in strength and courage.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，隨募至安西，頻經戰鬥，於時諸軍初用陌刀，咸推嗣業為能。

translations.literal: Early in the Tianbao era he volunteered and went to Anxi. He fought in many engagements. At that time the armies were first adopting the long-handled saber, and all acclaimed Siye as master of it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he volunteered and went to Anxi. He fought in many engagements. At that time the armies were first adopting the long-handled saber, and all acclaimed Siye as its master.

sentences.zh: 每為隊頭，所向必陷。

translations.literal: Whenever he served as squad leader, wherever he aimed he broke through.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he served as squad leader, wherever he aimed he broke through.

sentences.zh: 節度使馬靈察知其勇健，每出師，令嗣業與焉。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Ma Lingcha knew his bravery and strength and, whenever he took the field, had Siye accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Military Commissioner Ma Lingcha knew his bravery and strength and, whenever he took the field, had Siye accompany him.

sentences.zh: 累遷至中郎將。

translations.literal: He rose in successive promotions to Middle General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in successive promotions to Middle General.

sentences.zh: 天寶七載，安西都知兵馬使高仙芝奉詔總軍，專征勃律，選嗣業與郎將田珍為左右陌刀將。

translations.literal: In Tianbao 7, Anxi Chief Military Commissioner Gao Xianzhi received orders to command the army in a campaign devoted to Balur; he selected Siye and Commandant Tian Zhen as left and right long-saber generals.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 7, Anxi Chief Military Commissioner Gao Xianzhi received orders to command the army in a campaign against Balur. He selected Siye and Commandant Tian Zhen as left and right long-saber generals.

sentences.zh: 於時吐蕃聚十萬眾於娑勒城，據山因水，塹斷崖谷，編木為城。

translations.literal: At that time Tibet gathered a hundred thousand men at Suole City, taking the mountain and using the water, cutting trenches across cliff valleys, weaving timbers into a fortress.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tibet gathered a hundred thousand men at Suole City, taking the mountain and using the water, cutting trenches across cliff valleys, and weaving timbers into a fortress.

sentences.zh: 仙芝夜引軍渡信圖河，奄至城下。

translations.literal: Xianzhi led the army by night across the Xintu River and suddenly arrived below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi led the army by night across the Xintu River and suddenly arrived below the city.

sentences.zh: 仙芝謂嗣業與田珍曰：「不午時須破此賊。」

translations.literal: Xianzhi said to Siye and Tian Zhen: "Before noon this enemy must be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said to Siye and Tian Zhen, "Before noon this enemy must be broken."

sentences.zh: 嗣業引步軍持長刀上，山頭拋櫑蔽空而下，嗣業獨引一旗於絕險處先登，諸將因之齊上。

translations.literal: Siye led infantry bearing long swords uphill; from the mountaintop trebuchet stones filled the sky as they descended. Siye alone took one banner and was first to ascend at the most perilous spot; the other generals followed and charged together.
translations.idiomatic: Siye led infantry bearing long swords uphill while trebuchet stones from the mountaintop filled the sky. Siye alone took one banner and was first to ascend at the most perilous spot; the other generals followed and charged together.

sentences.zh: 賊不虞漢軍暴至，遂大潰，填溪谷，投水溺死，僅十八九。

translations.literal: The enemy did not expect Han troops to arrive so suddenly; they broke in utter rout, filling ravines and gullies, drowning as they cast themselves into the water — only one or two in ten survived.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did not expect Han troops to arrive so suddenly. They broke in utter rout, filling ravines and gullies and drowning as they cast themselves into the water — only one or two in ten survived.

sentences.zh: 遂長驅至勃律城擒勃律王、吐蕃公主，斬藤橋，以兵三千人戍。

translations.literal: They drove straight through to Balur city, captured the King of Balur and the Tibetan princess, cut the vine bridge, and left three thousand troops to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: They drove straight through to Balur city, captured the King of Balur and the Tibetan princess, cut the vine bridge, and left three thousand troops to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 於是拂林、大食諸胡七十二國皆歸國家，款塞朝獻，嗣業之功也。

translations.literal: Thereupon seventy-two states of the foreign peoples — among them Byzantium and the Arabs — all submitted to the state, came to the frontier with tribute, and sent missions to court — this was Siye's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon seventy-two foreign states — among them Byzantium and the Arabs — all submitted to the empire, came to the frontier with tribute, and sent missions to court. This was Siye's achievement.

sentences.zh: 由此拜右威衛將軍。

translations.literal: For this he was appointed General of the Right Majestic Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was appointed General of the Right Majestic Guard.

sentences.zh: 十載，又從平石國，及破九國胡並背叛突騎施，以跳蕩加特進，兼本官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again followed in the pacification of Shi Kingdom and in crushing the rebellious Nine-States Hu and the renegade Turgish. For his bold assault he received the special advancement Tejin while retaining his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he again followed in the pacification of Shi Kingdom and in crushing the rebellious Nine-States Hu and the renegade Turgish. For his bold assault he received the special advancement Tejin while retaining his original office.

sentences.zh: 初，仙芝紿石國王約為和好，乃將兵襲破之，殺其老弱，虜其丁壯，取金寶瑟瑟駝馬等，國人號哭，因掠石國王東，獻之於闕下。

translations.literal: At first Xianzhi deceived the King of Shi with a pledge of friendship, then led troops in a surprise attack and broke the kingdom, killing the old and weak, carrying off the able-bodied, and seizing gold, jewels, sésè horses, and the like. The people wailed in grief. He then seized the king of Shi and took him east to present at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xianzhi deceived the King of Shi with a pledge of friendship, then led troops in a surprise attack and broke the kingdom, killing the old and weak, carrying off the able-bodied, and seizing gold, jewels, sésè horses, and the like. The people wailed in grief. He then seized the king of Shi and took him east to present at the capital.

sentences.zh: 其子逃難奔走，告於諸胡國。

translations.literal: His son fled in distress and spread word among the various Hu states.
translations.idiomatic: His son fled in distress and spread word among the various Hu states.

sentences.zh: 群胡忿之，與大食連謀，將欲攻四鎮。

translations.literal: The Hu peoples were enraged and joined in conspiracy with the Arabs, preparing to attack the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu peoples were enraged and joined in conspiracy with the Arabs, preparing to attack the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 仙芝懼，領兵二萬深入胡地，與大食戰，仙芝大敗。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was afraid. He led twenty thousand troops deep into Hu territory and fought the Arabs. Xianzhi suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was afraid. He led twenty thousand troops deep into Hu territory and fought the Arabs, suffering a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 會夜，兩軍解，仙芝眾為大食所殺，存者不過數千。

translations.literal: Night fell and the two armies disengaged. Xianzhi's force was slaughtered by the Arabs; those who survived numbered no more than a few thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Night fell and the two armies disengaged. Xianzhi's force was slaughtered by the Arabs; those who survived numbered no more than a few thousand.

sentences.zh: 事窘，嗣業白仙芝曰：「將軍深入胡地，後絕救兵。

translations.literal: The situation was dire. Siye reported to Xianzhi: "The general has penetrated deep into Hu territory with reinforcements cut off behind.
translations.idiomatic: The situation was dire. Siye reported to Xianzhi, "The general has penetrated deep into Hu territory with reinforcements cut off behind.

sentences.zh: 今大食戰勝，諸胡知，必乘勝而並力事漢。

translations.literal: Now that the Arabs have won, once the Hu peoples learn of it they will surely take advantage of victory and unite their strength against Han.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Arabs have won, once the Hu peoples learn of it they will surely take advantage of victory and unite their strength against Han.

sentences.zh: 若全軍沒，嗣業與將軍俱為賊所虜，則何人歸報主？

translations.literal: If the entire army perishes and both Siye and the general are taken by the enemy, who will return to report to the sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: If the entire army perishes and both Siye and the general are taken by the enemy, who will return to report to the sovereign?

sentences.zh: 不如馳守白石嶺，早圖奔逸之計。」

translations.literal: Better to ride swiftly to hold Baishi Ridge and devise a plan for escape early."
translations.idiomatic: Better to ride swiftly to hold Baishi Ridge and devise a plan for escape early."

sentences.zh: 仙芝曰：「爾，戰將也。

translations.literal: Xianzhi said: "You are a fighting general.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi said, "You are a fighting general.

sentences.zh: 吾欲收合余燼，明日復戰，期一勝耳。」

translations.literal: I wish to gather the surviving embers and fight again tomorrow, seeking one victory."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to gather the surviving embers and fight again tomorrow, seeking one victory."

sentences.zh: 嗣業曰：「愚者千慮，或有一得，勢危若此，不可膠柱。」

translations.literal: Siye said: "Even the foolish may hit upon something in a thousand calculations; with danger this grave, one cannot cling rigidly to fixed plans."
translations.idiomatic: Siye said, "Even the foolish may hit upon something in a thousand calculations. With danger this grave, one cannot cling rigidly to fixed plans."

sentences.zh: 固請行，乃從之。

translations.literal: He pressed his request firmly, and Xianzhi at last acceded.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his request firmly, and Xianzhi at last acceded.

sentences.zh: 路隘，人馬魚貫而奔。

translations.literal: The road was narrow; men and horses fled single file like a string of fish.
translations.idiomatic: The road was narrow; men and horses fled single file like a string of fish.

sentences.zh: 會跋汗那兵眾先奔，人及駝馬塞路，不克過。

translations.literal: Just then the troops of Bohanna had fled ahead; men and camels blocked the road so passage was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the troops of Bohanna had fled ahead; men and camels blocked the road so passage was impossible.

sentences.zh: 嗣業持大棒前驅擊之，人馬應手俱斃。

translations.literal: Siye seized a great club and struck forward as vanguard; men and horses fell dead at each blow.
translations.idiomatic: Siye seized a great club and struck forward as vanguard; men and horses fell dead at each blow.

sentences.zh: 胡等遁，路開，仙芝獲免。

translations.literal: The Hu fled, the road cleared, and Xianzhi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu fled, the road cleared, and Xianzhi escaped.

sentences.zh: 仙芝表其功，加驃騎左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Xianzhi memorialized his merit and he was promoted to General of the Left Gold Crow Guard, Biaoqi rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi memorialized his merit and he was promoted to General of the Left Gold Crow Guard, Biaoqi rank.

sentences.zh: 及祿山反，兩京陷，上在靈武，詔嗣業赴行在。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled and the two capitals fell, the emperor was at Lingwu and ordered Siye to proceed to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled and the two capitals fell, the emperor was at Lingwu and ordered Siye to proceed to the temporary court.

sentences.zh: 嗣業自安西統眾萬里，威令肅然，所過郡縣，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Siye led his troops from Anxi ten thousand li; his authority was stern and orderly, and the commanderies and counties he passed through suffered not the slightest harm.
translations.idiomatic: Siye led his troops from Anxi ten thousand li. His authority was stern and orderly, and the commanderies and counties he passed through suffered not the slightest harm.

sentences.zh: 至鳳翔謁見，上曰：「今日得卿，勝數萬眾，事之濟否，實在卿也。」

translations.literal: Arriving at Fengxiang he had audience. The emperor said: "Today in gaining you I have gained the equal of tens of thousands. Whether this affair succeeds truly rests with you."
translations.idiomatic: Arriving at Fengxiang he had audience. The emperor said, "Today in gaining you I have gained the equal of tens of thousands. Whether this affair succeeds truly rests with you."

sentences.zh: 遂與郭子儀、仆固懷恩等常犄角為先鋒將。

translations.literal: Thereafter with Guo Ziyi, Pugu Huai'en, and others he regularly formed paired horns as vanguard general.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter with Guo Ziyi, Pugu Huai'en, and others he regularly served as vanguard general in paired formation.

sentences.zh: 嗣業每持大棒沖擊，賊眾披靡，所向無敵。

translations.literal: Siye always charged wielding his great club; rebel ranks broke before him and nowhere did he meet a match.
translations.idiomatic: Siye always charged wielding his great club; rebel ranks broke before him and nowhere did he meet a match.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，兩京未復，肅宗在鳳翔。

translations.literal: During Lushan's rebellion the two capitals had not yet been recovered; Emperor Suzong was at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: During Lushan's rebellion the two capitals had not yet been recovered; Emperor Suzong was at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 至德二年九月，嗣業從廣平王收復京城，與賊大戰於香積寺北，西拒灃水，東臨大川，十里間軍容不斷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Zhide 2, Siye followed the Prince of Guangping in recovering the capital. They fought a great battle with the rebels north of Xiangjisi Temple — the west barred by Feng River, the east facing a great stream; for ten li the battle lines were unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhide 2, Siye followed the Prince of Guangping in recovering the capital. They fought a great battle with the rebels north of Xiangjisi Temple — the west barred by Feng River, the east facing a great stream — and for ten li the battle lines were unbroken.

sentences.zh: 嗣業時為鎮西、北庭支度行營節度使，為前軍，朔方右行營節度使郭子儀為中軍，關內行營節度王思禮為後軍。

translations.literal: Siye then served as Military Commissioner of the Zhendi and Beiting Supply Expeditions as the vanguard; Guo Ziyi, Military Commissioner of the Right Shuofang Expedition, commanded the center; Wang Sili, Military Commissioner of the Guannei Expedition, the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Siye then served as Military Commissioner of the Zhendi and Beiting Supply Expeditions as the vanguard; Guo Ziyi, Military Commissioner of the Right Shuofang Expedition, commanded the center; and Wang Sili, Military Commissioner of the Guannei Expedition, the rear.

sentences.zh: 戈鋌鼓鞞，震曜山野，距賊軍數里，列長陣而待之。

translations.literal: Spears and halberds, drums and war hides — the glare shook mountain and field. Several li from the rebel army they deployed in a long battle line and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Spears and halberds, drums and war hides — the glare shook mountain and field. Several li from the rebel army they deployed in a long battle line and waited.

sentences.zh: 賊將李歸仁初以銳師數來挑戰，我師攢矢而逐之，賊軍大至，逼我追騎，突入我營，我師囂亂。

translations.literal: Rebel general Li Guiren first sent elite troops repeatedly to challenge. Our forces gathered arrows and pursued them. The rebel army arrived in force, pressed our pursuing horsemen, and burst into our camp — our army fell into uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Li Guiren first sent elite troops repeatedly to challenge. Our forces gathered arrows and pursued them. The rebel army arrived in force, pressed our pursuing horsemen, and burst into our camp — our army fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 嗣業謂郭子儀曰：「今日之事，若不以身啖寇，決戰於陣，萬死而冀其一生。

translations.literal: Siye said to Guo Ziyi: "In today's affair, unless we offer our bodies to feed the enemy and decide the battle in the ranks — ten thousand deaths hoping for one life —
translations.idiomatic: Siye said to Guo Ziyi, "In today's affair, unless we offer our bodies to feed the enemy and decide the battle in the ranks — ten thousand deaths hoping for one life —

sentences.zh: 不然，則我軍無孑遺矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise not one of our army will survive."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise not one of our army will survive."

sentences.zh: 嗣業乃脫衣徒搏，執長刀立於陣前大呼，當嗣業刀者，人馬俱碎，殺十數人，陣容方駐。

translations.literal: Siye stripped to the waist for bare-handed combat, grasped a long sword, stood before the battle line and shouted. Those who met Siye's blade — men and horses alike were shattered. He killed more than a dozen; only then did the formation steady.
translations.idiomatic: Siye stripped to the waist, grasped a long sword, stood before the battle line and shouted. Those who met Siye's blade — men and horses alike were shattered. He killed more than a dozen, and only then did the formation steady.

sentences.zh: 前軍之士盡執長刀而出，如墻而進。

translations.literal: The vanguard soldiers all took up long swords and advanced like a moving wall.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard soldiers all took up long swords and advanced like a moving wall.

sentences.zh: 嗣業先登奮命，所向摧靡。

translations.literal: Siye was first to ascend and fought with all his life; wherever he turned, resistance crumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Siye was first to ascend and fought with all his life; wherever he turned, resistance crumbled.

sentences.zh: 是時，賊先伏兵於營東，偵者知之，元帥廣平王分回紇銳卒，令擊其伏兵，賊將大敗。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels had hidden troops east of camp. Scouts discovered them. The commander, the Prince of Guangping, detached elite Uyghur soldiers to strike the ambush; the rebel generals were routed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebels had hidden troops east of camp. Scouts discovered them. The commander, the Prince of Guangping, detached elite Uyghur soldiers to strike the ambush, and the rebel generals were routed.

sentences.zh: 嗣業出賊營之背，與回紇合勢，表裏夾攻，自午及酉，斬首六萬級，填溝壑而死者十二三。

translations.literal: Siye emerged behind the rebel camp and joined forces with the Uyghurs in pincer attack from within and without. From noon until dusk they took sixty thousand heads; one or two in ten of those who fell filled ravines and ditches in death.
translations.idiomatic: Siye emerged behind the rebel camp and joined forces with the Uyghurs in pincer attack from within and without. From noon until dusk they took sixty thousand heads; one or two in ten of those who fell filled ravines and ditches in death.

sentences.zh: 賊帥張通儒、安守忠、李歸仁等收合殘卒，東走保陜郡。

translations.literal: Rebel commanders Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and others gathered the remnants and fled east to hold Shaan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel commanders Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and others gathered the remnants and fled east to hold Shaan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 慶緒又命嚴莊率眾數萬，赴陜助通儒輩以拒官軍。

translations.literal: Qingxu also ordered Yan Zhuang to lead tens of thousands to go to Shaan and assist Tongru's group in resisting the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu also ordered Yan Zhuang to lead tens of thousands to Shaan to assist Tongru's group in resisting the government army.

sentences.zh: 廣平王、郭子儀、王思禮等大軍營於陜西。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping, Guo Ziyi, Wang Sili, and the main army encamped west of Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping, Guo Ziyi, Wang Sili, and the main army encamped west of Shaan.

sentences.zh: 嗣業與子儀遇賊於新店，與之力戰，數合，我師初勝而後敗，嗣業逐急應接。

translations.literal: Siye and Ziyi encountered the enemy at Xindian and fought them fiercely through several engagements. Our army at first won and then lost; Siye pressed hard amid the emergency to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Siye and Ziyi encountered the enemy at Xindian and fought them fiercely through several engagements. Our army at first won and then lost; Siye pressed hard amid the emergency to respond.

sentences.zh: 回紇從南山望見官軍敗，曳白旗而下，徑抵賊背，穿賊陣，賊陣西北角先陷。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs from the southern hills saw the government army losing and descended trailing white banners, going straight to the rebel rear and piercing their battle line — the northwest corner of the rebel formation broke first.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs from the southern hills saw the government army losing and descended trailing white banners, going straight to the rebel rear and piercing their battle line — the northwest corner of the rebel formation broke first.

sentences.zh: 嗣業又率精騎前擊，表裏齊進，賊眾大敗，走河北。

translations.literal: Siye again led elite cavalry in a forward assault; inner and outer forces advanced together and the rebel masses were routed, fleeing north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Siye again led elite cavalry in a forward assault; inner and outer forces advanced together and the rebel masses were routed, fleeing north of the river.

sentences.zh: 子儀遂收東都。

translations.literal: Ziyi thereupon recovered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi thereupon recovered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 嗣業以功加開府儀同三司、衛尉卿，封虢國公，食實封二百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit Siye received the additional honors of Grand Mentor with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and Minister of Guardians; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Guo with two hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Siye received the additional honors of Grand Mentor with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and Minister of Guardians; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Guo with two hundred actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，諸將同圍相州。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan 2 the generals jointly besieged Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 2 the generals jointly besieged Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時築堤引漳水灌城，經月余，城不拔。

translations.literal: At that time they built dikes to divert Zhang River water to flood the city. After more than a month the city still was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: At that time they built dikes to divert Zhang River water to flood the city. After more than a month the city still was not taken.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍無統帥，諸將自圖全，人無鬥志。

translations.literal: At that time the army had no commander-in-chief; each general sought his own safety and the men lacked fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the army had no commander-in-chief; each general sought his own safety and the men lacked fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 賊每出戰，嗣業被堅沖突，履鋒冒刃，為流矢所中。

translations.literal: Whenever the rebels came out to fight, Siye donned heavy armor and charged forward, treading blades and braving edges, and was struck by stray arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the rebels came out to fight, Siye donned heavy armor and charged forward, treading blades and braving edges, and was struck by stray arrows.

sentences.zh: 數日，瘡欲愈，臥於帳中，忽聞金鼓之聲，因而大叫，瘡中血出數升注地而卒。

translations.literal: Several days later his wounds were nearly healed. Lying in his tent he suddenly heard the sound of gongs and drums; he cried out at once, and blood poured several sheng from his wounds onto the ground — and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later his wounds were nearly healed. Lying in his tent he suddenly heard the sound of gongs and drums; he cried out at once, and blood poured several sheng from his wounds onto the ground — and he died.

sentences.zh: 上聞之震悼，嗟惜久之，詔曰：「臨難忘身，為臣之大節；

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he was deeply shaken and grieved and sighed in lament for a long time. An edict read: "Facing peril without forgetting one's body — this is the great principle of a minister;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was deeply shaken and grieved and sighed in lament for a long time. An edict read: "Facing peril without forgetting one's body — this is the great principle of a minister;

sentences.zh: 念功加贈，經國之常典。

translations.literal: remembering merit with posthumous honors — this is the constant practice of governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: remembering merit with posthumous honors — this is the constant practice of governing the state.

sentences.zh: 故衛尉卿、兼懷州刺史、充北庭行營節度使、虢國公李嗣業，植操沈厚，秉心忠烈，懷幹時之勇略，有戡難之遠謀。

translations.literal: The late Commandant of the Guard, concurrently Prefect of Huaizhou, commissioned as Military Commissioner of the Beiting Field Headquarters, and Duke of the State of Guo, Li Siye — rooted in bearing, deep and steadfast, holding a heart loyal and resolute, possessing timely courage and strategy, and having far-reaching plans for quelling disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The late Commandant of the Guard Li Siye, Duke of the State of Guo, had also served as Prefect of Huaizhou and Military Commissioner of the Beiting Field Headquarters. Steadfast in character, deep and unwavering, he bore a loyal and resolute heart and possessed both the courage and strategy the times demanded and far-reaching plans for quelling calamity.

sentences.zh: 久仕邊陲，備經任使。

translations.literal: He served long on the frontier borders and fully experienced every assignment and commission.
translations.idiomatic: He had long served on the frontier and had seen every sort of assignment through.

sentences.zh: 自兇渠構亂，中夏不寧，持感激之誠，總驍果之眾，親當矢石，頻立勛庸。

translations.literal: Since the ringleader of rebellion stirred disorder and the Central Lands knew no peace, he held a heart stirred to gratitude, gathered a host of fierce and resolute men, personally met flying arrows and stones, and repeatedly established meritorious deeds.
translations.idiomatic: From the day the rebel chieftain stirred chaos and the heartland knew no peace, he served with grateful devotion, rallied fierce and resolute troops, braved arrows and stones in person, and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 壯節可嘉，將謀於百勝；

translations.literal: His stalwart integrity was worthy of praise; he was about to plan for victory in a hundred battles;
translations.idiomatic: His stalwart integrity deserved all praise, and he was poised to plan triumph upon triumph;

sentences.zh: 忠誠未遂，空恨於九原。

translations.literal: Yet his loyal devotion went unfulfilled, leaving only empty regret in the nine plains.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his loyal devotion remained unfulfilled, and he carried only futile regret to the grave.

sentences.zh: 言念其功，良深憫悼。

translations.literal: Thinking of his merit, We are deeply moved to pity and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When We consider his merit, Our pity and mourning run deep.

sentences.zh: 死於王事，禮有可加，宜贈裂土之封，用廣飾終之義。

translations.literal: Dying in the sovereign's service — rites allow addition; he should be granted a fief entailing land, to extend the meaning of rites that adorn the dead.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sovereign's service, and the rites permit further honor: let there be granted a fief entailing land, that the rites due the dead may be amply observed.

sentences.zh: 可贈武威郡王。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其賻贈及緣葬事，所司倍於常式，仍令官給靈輿，遞還所在。

translations.literal: As for funeral gifts and matters connected with burial, the responsible offices shall double the usual standard; let an official funeral carriage also be provided and escorted by relay back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: For funeral gifts and all matters connected with his burial, the responsible offices shall observe double the usual standard, and an official funeral carriage shall be furnished and escorted by relay to his home district.

sentences.zh: 以其子佐國襲其官爵，食實封二百戶。」

translations.literal: Let his son Zuoguo inherit his office and title, with a substantive fief of two hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuoguo shall inherit his office and title, with a substantive fief of two hundred households."

sentences.zh: 白孝德，安西胡人也，驍悍有膽力。

translations.literal: Bai Xiaode — a Hu native of Anxi, fierce and bold, possessed of courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Xiaode was a Hu native of Anxi, fierce and bold, and possessed of great courage and strength.

sentences.zh: 乾元中，事李光弼為偏裨。

translations.literal: In the Qianyuan era he served Li Guangbi as a junior commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyuan era he served under Li Guangbi as a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 史思明攻河陽，使驍將劉龍仙率鐵騎五千臨城挑戰。

translations.literal: Shi Siming attacked Heyang and sent the fierce general Liu Longxian at the head of five thousand iron horsemen to ride up to the walls and offer challenge.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming attacked Heyang, he sent his fierce general Liu Longxian at the head of five thousand armored horsemen to ride up beneath the walls and issue a challenge.

sentences.zh: 龍仙捷勇自恃，舉右足加馬鬣上，嫚罵光弼。

translations.literal: Longxian relied on his swiftness and bravery; he raised his right foot and set it atop his horse's mane and reviled Guangbi with insults.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his swiftness and courage, Longxian planted his right foot atop his horse's mane and showered Guangbi with insults.

sentences.zh: 光弼登城望，顧諸將曰：「孰可取者？」

translations.literal: Guangbi ascended the wall to look out. Turning to the generals he said: "Who can take him?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi climbed the wall to look out. Turning to his generals he said, "Who can take him?"

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩請行，光弼曰：「此非大將所為。」

translations.literal: Pugu Huaien asked to go. Guangbi said: "This is not work for a grand general."
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huaien volunteered. Guangbi said, "This is not work for a grand general."

sentences.zh: 歷選其次，左右曰：「白孝德可。」

translations.literal: They went down the list in turn; those beside him said: "Bai Xiaode will do."
translations.idiomatic: They went down the list in turn; those beside him said, "Bai Xiaode will do."

sentences.zh: 光弼乃招孝德前，問曰：「可乎？」

translations.literal: Guangbi then summoned Xiaode forward and asked: "Will it work?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi then summoned Xiaode forward and asked, "Will it work?"

translations.literal: He said: "It will."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "It will."

sentences.zh: 光弼問：「所要幾何兵？」

translations.literal: Guangbi asked: "How many troops do you need?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi asked, "How many troops do you need?"

sentences.zh: 孝德曰：「可獨往耳。」

translations.literal: Xiaode said: "I can go alone."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode said, "I can go alone."

sentences.zh: 光弼壯之。

translations.literal: Guangbi admired his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi admired his daring.

sentences.zh: 終問所欲，對曰：「願選五十騎於軍門為繼，兼請大軍鼓噪以增氣勢，他無所用。」

translations.literal: When he finally asked what Xiaode wanted, he replied: "I wish to select fifty horsemen at the army gate as reinforcements, and also ask that the main army raise a battle clamor to swell the momentum — nothing else is needed."
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbi finally asked what he wanted, Xiaode replied, "Let me choose fifty horsemen at the army gate as reinforcements, and ask that the main army raise a battle clamor to swell our momentum — nothing else is needed."

sentences.zh: 光弼撫其背以遣之。

translations.literal: Guangbi clapped his back and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi clapped him on the back and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 孝德挾二矛，策馬截流而渡。

translations.literal: Xiaode tucked two spears under his arms and spurred his horse to ford the stream at a crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode tucked two spears under his arms and spurred his horse across the ford.

sentences.zh: 半濟，懷恩賀曰：「克矣。」

translations.literal: Halfway across, Huaien congratulated him: "He is taken!"
translations.idiomatic: Halfway across, Huaien cried, "He is taken!"

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「未及，何知其克？」

translations.literal: Guangbi said: "Not yet — how do you know he is taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi said, "Not yet — how do you know he is taken?"

sentences.zh: 懷恩曰：「觀其攬轡便辟，可萬全者。」

translations.literal: Huaien said: "Watch how he gathers the reins and adapts his seat — that is a man who can be absolutely sure of victory."
translations.idiomatic: Huaien said, "See how he gathers the reins and adapts his seat — that is a man who can be absolutely sure of victory."

sentences.zh: 龍仙見其獨來，甚易之，足不降鬣。

translations.literal: Longxian saw him come alone and thought him an easy mark; he did not lower his foot from the mane.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian saw him come alone and thought him an easy mark; he did not lower his foot from the mane.

sentences.zh: 稍近，將動，孝德搖手示之，若使其不動，龍仙不之測，乃止。

translations.literal: As he drew nearer and was about to move, Xiaode waved his hand at him, as if telling him not to move; Longxian could not fathom it and so held still.
translations.idiomatic: As he drew nearer and was about to move, Xiaode waved his hand at him as if to tell him to hold still; Longxian could not fathom it and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 孝德呼曰：「侍中使余致辭，非他也。」

translations.literal: Xiaode called out: "The chief minister sends me to convey words — it is nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode called out, "The chief minister sends me to convey words — nothing more."

sentences.zh: 龍仙去十步與之言，褻罵如初。

translations.literal: Longxian came ten paces forward to speak with him, reviling him with vulgar abuse as before.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian came ten paces forward to speak with him and reviled him with vulgar abuse as before.

sentences.zh: 孝德息馬伺便，因瞋目曰：「賊識我乎？」

translations.literal: Xiaode rested his horse waiting for his chance; then with a glare he said: "Do you, bandit, know me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode rested his horse, waiting for his opening; then with a glare he said, "Do you, bandit, know me?"

sentences.zh: 龍仙曰：「誰耶？」

translations.literal: Longxian said: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Longxian said, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「我，國之大將白孝德也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I am Bai Xiaode, a great general of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I am Bai Xiaode, a great general of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 龍仙曰：「是何豬狗！」

translations.literal: Longxian said: "What kind of swine and cur are you?!"
translations.idiomatic: Longxian said, "What kind of swine and cur are you?!"

sentences.zh: 孝德發聲寔啖，持矛躍馬而搏之。

translations.literal: Xiaode let out a battle roar, seized his spear, leaped on his horse and closed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode let out a battle roar, seized his spear, spurred his horse forward and closed with him.

sentences.zh: 城上鼓噪，五十騎繼進。

translations.literal: On the wall they raised the battle clamor; the fifty horsemen followed in support.
translations.idiomatic: On the walls the army raised a battle clamor, and the fifty horsemen followed in support.

sentences.zh: 龍仙矢不暇發，環走堤上。

translations.literal: Longxian had no time to loose his arrows and circled along the embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Longxian had no time to loose his arrows and circled along the embankment.

sentences.zh: 孝德追及，斬首，攜之而歸，賊徒大駭。

translations.literal: Xiaode caught up with him, cut off his head, and carried it back; the bandits were utterly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaode caught up with him, cut off his head, and carried it back; the rebel troops were utterly terrified.

sentences.zh: 其後，累戰功至安西北庭行營節度、鄜坊邠寧節度使，歷檢校刑部尚書，封昌化郡王。

translations.literal: Thereafter he accumulated battle merit until he became Military Commissioner of the Anxi-Beiting Field Headquarters and of Fufang Binning, successively served as Acting Minister of Justice, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Changhua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he accumulated battle honors until he became Military Commissioner of the Anxi-Beiting Field Headquarters and of Fufang Binning, served successively as Acting Minister of Justice, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Changhua Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以家難去職，服闋復舊官。

translations.literal: He left office on account of family mourning; when the mourning period ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on account of family mourning, and when the mourning period ended he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年九月，轉太子少傅，尋卒，時年六十六，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year of Dali he was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; soon afterward he died, at age sixty-six, and was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Dali 14 he was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; soon afterward he died at age sixty-six and was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：歷代武臣，壯勇出眾者有諸，節行勵俗者鮮矣，矧蠻夷之人乎！

translations.literal: The court historian writes: Throughout the ages among military officers, many have stood out for bold courage, but few have cultivated integrity that admonishes custom — how much less among barbarian peoples!
translations.idiomatic: The court historian writes: Throughout the ages, many military officers have stood out for bold courage, but few have cultivated conduct that admonishes custom — how much less among barbarian peoples!

sentences.zh: 如馮盎智勇守節，社尒廉慎知足，蘇尼失恩惠，史忠清謹。

translations.literal: Such as Feng Ang with wisdom and courage who upheld integrity, She'er who was frugal and cautious and content, Sunishi who showed kindness and grace, and Zhong who was pure and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Feng Ang, wise and courageous, who upheld his integrity; She'er, frugal, cautious, and content; Sunishi, generous and gracious; and Zhong, pure and careful.

sentences.zh: 凡用兵破吐蕃、谷渾，勇也；

translations.literal: In general — in campaigning to break Tibet and Tuyuhun, there was courage;
translations.idiomatic: In campaigning to break Tibet and Tuyuhun — that was courage;

sentences.zh: 心如鐵石，忠也；

translations.literal: a heart like iron and stone — there was loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: a heart like iron and stone — that was loyalty;

sentences.zh: 不解萬均官，恕也；

translations.literal: refusing to strip Wanjun of his office — there was forbearance;
translations.idiomatic: refusing to strip Wanjun of his office — that was forbearance;

sentences.zh: 阻延陀之親，智也；

translations.literal: blocking alliance with the Tiele — there was wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: blocking alliance with the Tiele — that was wisdom;

sentences.zh: 舍高突勃之死，識也。

translations.literal: renouncing the death of Gao Tubo — there was discernment.
translations.idiomatic: renouncing the death of Gao Tubo — that was discernment.

sentences.zh: 立大功，居顯位，夙夜匪懈者，何力有焉。

translations.literal: To establish great merit, hold exalted rank, and never slacken day or night — what force was his equal?
translations.idiomatic: To establish great merit, hold exalted rank, and never slacken day or night — what man could match Qibi Heli?

sentences.zh: 常之以私馬恕官兵，與將士均賞賜，古之名將，無以加焉。

translations.literal: Changzhi forgave his officers and men with his private horses and shared rewards equally with the soldiers — among famed generals of old, none can surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi pardoned his officers and men with his private horses and shared rewards equally with his soldiers — among famed generals of old, none can surpass him.

sentences.zh: 多祚忘身許國，孝德壯勇立功，皆三軍之傑也，豈九夷之陋哉！

translations.literal: Duozuo forgot himself in service to the state, Xiaode with bold courage established merit — all were champions of the three armies; how could they be the baseness of the Nine Yi!
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo forgot himself in service to the state, and Xiaode with bold courage won distinction — all were champions of the three armies. How could they be the baseness of the Nine Yi!

sentences.zh: 嗣業力贊中興，終歿王事，未可倫而擬也。

translations.literal: Siye powerfully aided the restoration, and at last died in the sovereign's service — he cannot be ranked alongside or compared to the others.
translations.idiomatic: Siye powerfully aided the restoration and at last died in the sovereign's service — he cannot be ranked alongside or compared to the others.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：君子之居，九夷無陋。

translations.literal: The praise reads: "Where the noble man dwells, even the Nine Yi are not base."
translations.idiomatic: The praise reads: "Where the noble man dwells, even the Nine Yi are not base."

sentences.zh: 壯哉嗣業，孰出其右！

translations.literal: How mighty was Siye — who could stand to his right!
translations.idiomatic: How mighty was Siye — who could stand to his right!
